questions.subject: History
questions.question: From which one of the following sites have bone implements been found?
questions.explanation: A large number of implements made of bones and horns have been found from the Mesolithic site, Mahadaha and Sarai Nahar Rai (located in Pratapgarh district of U.P.). The book titled ‘Puratattva Vimarsh ‘ written by Dr. Jai Narayan Pandey describes various pointed objects and ornaments made of bones that have been reported from Sarai Nahar Rai, Damdama and Mahadaha.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Three human skeletons in a single grave were recovered at –
questions.explanation: Damdama is a Mesolithic site in Pratapgarh district Uttar Pradesh. In Damdama, 41 human graves were found. Out of these graves, 5 are double burials. One triple burial grave is also found here. A grave with four human skeletons has been found at Sarai Nahar Rai.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The cultivation of cereals first started in -
questions.explanation: Grains were first produced in the Neolithic Age. It was the time when people were introduced to agriculture. Koldihwa and Mehrgarh were the two Neolithic archaeological sites from where clear pieces of evidence of rice and wheat have been found.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The first cereal used by man was :
questions.explanation: There are mainly eight types of food grains consumed by modern human society, namely barley, wheat, maize, millet, sorghum, mustard, oat and rice. These plants were present in the form of weeds in different areas, which were later grown as seeds by humans at different places, and at different times. Although, barley was the first grain to be cultivated by human beings around 8000 B.C. in western Asian countries located between the northeast Mediterranean Sea and Iran. Later, in the same area, wheat was also cultivated around 8000 B.C.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The earliest evidence of agriculture in Indian sub-continent comes from –
questions.explanation: According to the latest research, the earliest evidence of agriculture in Indian subcontinent has been reported from the Lahuradeva site in Sant Kabir Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh. The evidence of human activity and beginning of rice cultivation at this site dates back to around 9000-7000 B.C. Significantly before this research, earlier evidence of wheat was found at Mehrgarh (located in Balochistan, Pakistan) belonging to around 7000 B.C. and the earliest evidence of rice is known to be near the bank of the river Belan, in district Prayagraj, from where rice bran was found dating back to 6500 B.C. With above reference, if Lahuradeva is one option, then it will be the correct answer, but if Lahuradeva is not an option, then Mehrgarh would be the right answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Name the site which has revealed the earliest evidence of settled life?
questions.explanation: Among the given options, the oldest evidence of permanent life has been found for the first time from Mehrgarh located in Kachhi plains of Balochistan, whose authentic date is around 7000 B.C., while the oldest date for Kile Gul Muhammad and Kalibangan are 4000 B.C. and 3500 B.C. respectively. Hence option (d) is correct option.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Excavation at Navadatoli was conducted by –
questions.explanation: Navdatoli has revealed excellent evidence of both round and rectangular residential structures which are located near Khargone (Madhya Pradesh). The former measures about 3m in diameter and the latter 2m × 2.2m. The roofs were probably made of hay, branches and leaves and were supported on massive wooden posts, 22cm in diameter, raised at regular intervals around the huts. The open spaces between the posts were provided with mud-plastered bamboo screens. The house floors were made up of silt clay and river gravel, with the surface coated with lime. The huts were provided with one or two-mouthed ‘chulhas’ as well as storage jars and other earthen vessels. This site was excavated by Mr. H.D. Sankalia, Professor of Deccan College, Pune. This site was the most extensively excavated Chalcolithic site of Indian subcontinent, which is determined to be between 1500 B.C. and 1300 B.C. * In which state, is Navdatoli located ? [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2009] - Madhya Pradesh

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Megaliths have been identified as-
questions.explanation: The megaliths usually refer to the burials made up of large stones in graveyards away from the habitation area. A large fraction of these is assumed to be associated with burial or post-burial rituals including memorials for those whose remains may or may not be available. few types of these are; Chamber tombs, Dolmens, Stone alignments, Stone circles (cromlech), Pit-circles, etc.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ash mound is associated with the Neolithic site at –
questions.explanation: The ‘Ash mounds’ have been found from a Neolithic site Sangana Kallu located in Bellari district in Karnataka. They have also been found in Piklihal and Utnur. These ash mounds are the burnt relics of seasonal camps of Neolithic herdsmen community.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following places is famous for pre-historic paintings ?
questions.explanation: The rock shelters of Bhimbetka are located in Raisen (M.P.). UNESCO has included the shell pictures of Bhimbetka in the list of its world heritage sites. These caves exhibit the earliest traces of human life on the Indian subcontinent and include pictures of an elephant, sambhar, deer, etc. There are 500 pictures in approx. 700 rock shelters. * In India, from which rock-shelter, have pictures been found the most? [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2008] - Bhimbetka * Which Indian Archaeologist first visited 'Bhimbetka Caves' and discovered prehistoric significance of its rock paintings? [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2020] - V.S. Wakankar

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Ochre-coloured Pottery (O.C.P.) was christened at:
questions.explanation: Discovery and naming (christening) of OCP was done by B.B. Lal in 1950-52 at Hastinapur. Ochre-Coloured Pottery (known to archaeologists as OCP) has, as the name implies, its main distinguishing feature as its ochre colour, which gives it a first appearance of being badly fired. Other characteristics are its porous nature and the fact that it is invariably worn out at the edges.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the Chalcolithic period people of Maharashtra buried their dead under the floor of their houses in the following orientation:
questions.explanation: The people of Jorwe culture lived in large rectangular houses with wattle and daub walls and thatched roofs. They believed in life after death and therefore buried the dead inside the houses under the floor. Children were buried in two urns that were joined mouth-to-mouth and set horizontally in the pit, while adults were placed in a supine position with the head towards the north (north to south). These sites were found in Daimabad, Inamgaon, Chandoli, Nevasa, etc.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following sites has yielded skeleton of the dog along with human skeleton in burial ?
questions.explanation: The Burzahom site is a prehistoric settlement in the village of the same name in Kashmir Valley. Both human and animal skeletons were found here with trepanning (bored hole) marks. In many pits, bones of dogs and antlered deer were found along with human skeletons. The skeletons of humans were found in the burial pits in a sitting position along with bones of animals. The first excavation at the Burzahom site was carried out by Helmut de Terra and Dr. Thomas Paterson in the year 1935. * The evidence of pit dwelling has been obtained from [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011] -Burzahom

questions.explanation: According to 'Puratatva Vimarsh' by J.N. Pandey 17 human skeletons were obtained from rock shelter 1 of Lekhahiya in the Vindhya region. Some of these were in relatively pristine condition while most of the others were warped. According to John R. Lucas of University of Oregon (USA), remnants of 27 human skeletons were found in Lekhahiya.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : The stone age people of the Vindhyas migrated to the Ganga Valley in terminal Pleistocene period. Reason (R) :Due to climatic change, it was dry phase in this period. Choose the correct answer from the code given below. Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Stone age people of the Vindhyas migrated to the Ganga Valley in terminal Pleistocene period because of climatic change Vindhyan Valley had become dry. Due to climate change, it was dry phase in this period. Thus both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Indus Civilization existed in–
questions.explanation: The historical period is determined with respect to the available written literature. The period before which knowledge of the art of writing was not available is called early historical age. Indus Civilization is Proto historical civilization although the writing was known during this period, but it is still to be deciphered.

questions.question: Indus Valley civilization was Non-Aryan because -

options.d: It extended up to the Narmada valley

questions.explanation: Indus Valley Civilization was the earliest known urban civilization of Indian subcontinent whereas Aryan Civilization was rural civilization.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The important reason to keep Indus-Valley civilization before Aryan civilization is –
questions.explanation: The knowledge of script and town planning of Indus Valley Civilization was more developed than that of Pre-Aryans. Different archaeological pieces of evidence of pottery have been found in the early settlements of Mehrgarh from the Indus Valley Civilization. Pottery found during excavations proves that Indus Valley Civilization existed before Aryan Civilization. The red potteries painted with black figures were the speciality of Harappan Civilization, whereas the grey painted potteries were used by Aryans.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Indus Valley culture was different from the Vedic Civilization because

options.a: It had the amenities of developed city life
options.c: It lacked knowledge of iron and defensive arrow

questions.explanation: The culture of the Indus Valley Civilization was different from the Vedic culture in many ways. The Indus Valley Civilization was urban while the Vedic culture was rural. The script of Indus Valley Civilization was of depictive expressions. The people of Indus Valley Civilization did not know the use of iron, whereas the people of Vedic Civilization used iron weapons extensively.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The source of knowledge about Harappan culture is:
questions.explanation: The first artefact uncovered in Harappa was a unique stone seal carved with a unicorn and an inscription. Similar seals with different animal symbols and writings have been found through-out the region. Although the writing has not yet been deciphered, evidence found during the early archaeological excavations is the major source to know about the Harappan culture.

questions.question: The first archaeologist who excavated Harappa, but could not recognize its significance, was :
questions.explanation: Alexander Cunningham, who headed the Archaeological Survey of India, visited this site in 1853 A.D. and 1856 A.D. Cunningham made a few small excavations at the site and reported some discoveries of ancient pottery, stone, tools and a stone seal but did not recognize its significance. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Mohenjodaro and Harappa cities are dead now. Reason (R) : They were discovered during excavations. In the context of the above, which one of the following is correct? Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Mohenjodaro (now in Pakistan) is in the Larkana district of Sindh province on the right bank of the Indus river. Harappa is located in the Sahiwal district of Punjab province of Pakistan. Rakhaldas Banerjee and Dayaram Sahni were the two archaeologists who excavated the two major cities of Indus Valley Civilization. At present, these towns are extinct. Therefore, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) both are correct, but the reason is not the correct explanation. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: From where the evidence of rock-cut architecture was found, with reference to Harappa civilization?
questions.explanation: Dholavira, which is the second largest site of Harappan Civilization in India (after Rakhigarhi) is located in Rann of Kutch (Gujarat). R.S. Bisht and his colleagues excavated this site in 1992. Dholavira is one of the most prominent archaeological sites of Harappa which gives us important information about great bath and rock-cut reservoir which was 7 metres deep and 79 metres long. * Dholavira is located in the State of [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2010] - Gujarat

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Harappan city is divided into three parts?
questions.explanation: Dholavira is a Harappan site located in Kutch district of Gujarat. The town was built in a rectangular shape. It was divided into three parts-Citadel, Middle Town and Lower Town.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: A highly advanced water management system of Harappan times has been unearthed at–
questions.explanation: From Dholavira, a huge Rock-cut reservoir is found, whose size is about 79 × 12 m and 7 meters deep, having a huge capacity to store water. People of Dholavira were familiar with the advanced water management system. From the earliest evidence, people used to store water in this reservoir by building dams.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following sites has yielded evidence of a double burial?
questions.explanation: The evidence of three double burials has been found from Lothal. It was an important port of the Harappan culture. The evidence of double burials has also been found from Kalibangan and Rakhigarhi.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Recently, from excavations of Harappan site Sonauli what was found ?
questions.explanation: Sinauli is an archaeological site located in Baraut Tehsil, Baghpat district, Uttar Pradesh, where 125 graves belonging to Indus Valley Civilization were found. These graves are oriented in a North-South direction and most are identified as primary human burials. Some of the burials are found with animal bones and gold, copper and bangles.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: For clothing, cotton cultivation was first introduced in–
questions.explanation: Cotton was first cultivated in India for clothing. In 1922, Rakhal Das Banerjee took interest in the site of Mohenjo-Daro for excavation. Evidence of the earliest cotton cultivation was found by excavation in India. From India, it reached Greece where it was called as “Sindon”. The cotton cultivation in India started in 3000 B.C. while it was cultivated in Egypt in 2500 B.C.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following animals is not depicted on the Harappan seal ?
questions.explanation: People of Harappa civilization were known to horses, but no pieces of evidence have been found on seals. A great majority of seals found in Indus valley civilization carry short inscriptions with figures of the one-horned animal (most common), the Buffalo, the Tiger, the Rhinoceros, the Goat and the Elephant.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: A horned deity engraved on a terracotta cake has been recovered from
questions.explanation: From excavations at Kalibangan, a series of ‘fire altars’ on mud-brick platforms were discovered. A triangular terracotta cake found at Kalibangan had a carving of a horned deity on one side and an animal (goat) being dragged by a rope by a human on the other. This shows the way to the emergence of a sacrificial tradition in the entire era.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The beginning of idol worship is to be considered in –
questions.explanation: The pre-Aryan period is considered as the beginning of idol worship. Idol worship was prevalent in Indus Civilization and it is evident from the coins discovered from Mohenjodaro having the seal of God. They probably worshipped Mother Goddess in addition to male and female deities.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following civilizations flourished on the bank of River Nile ?
questions.explanation: Ancient Egyptian Civilization flourished along the banks of the River Nile for almost 3,000 years. Nile River is known as ‘lifeline of Egypt.’ The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeastern Africa, generally regarded as the longest river in the world. Indus Valley Civilization (India) and Mesopotamia (Iraq) are the contemporary civilization.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the correct North-South sequence of the following civilizations?
questions.explanation: The correct sequence of the following civilization from North to South is: Aztec - Maya- Moisca - Inca.The expansion of Aztec civilization was on the Northern Part of Mesoamerica. Mesoamerica included the Region from central Mexico, Beliz, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Norhtern Costarica. Mayan civilization was spread over the southern part of Mesoamerica. Moisca civilization was distributed in the eastern part of Columbia (South America continent), whereas Inca civilization is spread in the western part of southern America till the north of Quito and Santiago to the South.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The term ‘Aryan’ denotes :
questions.explanation: 'Aryan' is a term meaning 'noble' which was used as a self-designation by Indo-Iranian people. In classic Sanskrit the word Arya means- 'A nobleman'. The word was used by the people of the Vedic period in India as an ethnic label for themselves as well as to refer noble class. Scholars point out that even in ancient times, the idea of being an 'Aryan' was religious, cultural and linguistic, not racial.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Meaning of the term ‘Arya’ in classical Sanskrit is
questions.explanation: See the explanation of above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is oldest Veda :
questions.explanation: In Indian literature, Vedas are the most ancient scriptures which are four in number, namely Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda. Rigveda is the most important and oldest among all these.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Trayi’ is a name for –
questions.explanation: Rig Veda, Yajurveda and Samaveda are called Vedatrayi or simply Trayi.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List- I with List- II and select the correct answer from the codes given below : List- I List- II A. Rig Veda 1. Musical hymns B. Yajurveda 2. Hymns and rituals C. Samaveda 3. Charms and spells D. Atharvaveda 4. Hymns and prayers Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: Rigveda consists of 1028 hymns and 10552 verses or mantras or shlokas. Yajurveda contains the description of stotras and recitals. The Samaveda consists of many hymns which are taken from Rig Veda and are indeed lyrical and melodious. The Atharvaveda contains a lot of knowledge of the physical world and spirituality. * The Rig Veda is the [U.P. R.O./ A.R.O. (Pre) 2016] - Collection of hymns

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The compilation of which among the following is based upon the Rig Veda?
questions.explanation: The Samaveda is shortest among all the four Vedas. It is closely connected with the Rig Veda. It has taken many verses from the Rig Veda. The Samaveda is compiled inclusively for ritual application and all of its verses are meant to be chanted in ceremonies. Samaveda Samhita consists a total of 1875 verses. Amongst these except 75 or 99 verses, all of them are compiled in Rig Veda.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of the Vedic literature?
questions.explanation: Each of the Vedas is divided into four parts (or the sections). The correct order of them is Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads. Samhitas and Brahmanas form the Karma-Kanda segment of the Vedas. Aranyakas and Upanishads form the Gyan-Kanda segment of the Vedas. They explicitly focus on philosophy and spirituality.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Gopatha Brahmana’ is associated with –
questions.explanation: The Gopatha Brahmana is the only Brahmana, a genre of prose texts describing the Vedic rituals, associated with the Atharvaveda. The text is associated with both the Shaunaka and the Paippalada recensions of the Atharvaveda.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is a Samhita of Shukla Yajurveda?
questions.explanation: There are two branches of Yajurveda-Shukla Yajurveda and Krishna Yajurveda. Vajasneyi is the Samhita of Shukla Yajurveda. Shukla Yajurveda is available only in the poetic form whereas Krishna Yajurveda contains both poetic as well as prose forms.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Upanishads are books on –
questions.explanation: The Upanishad literature is not a religious scripture but represents a philosophy for all times and for all. The philosophy of Upanishads does not oppose any school of thought, religion or interpretation of the scriptures, but its method for explaining its concepts is unique. Upanishad means pupils sit near the teacher to learn from him about the secret doctrine.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following Vedic literatures talks about salvation :
questions.explanation: The word salvation or Moksha is not used in Vedas. It was first discussed in Upanishads. Moksha means ‘‘liberation’’. The continuous cycle of life and death is not the actual aim of the human soul. According to the Upanishads, the core of our self is not the body or the mind but the Atman (Soul).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The famous dialogue between Nachiketa and Yama is mentioned in the :
questions.explanation: Kathopanishad is the story of the conversation between Yama, Lord of death and Nachiketa, the young 12 year old boy, who left home in search of the meaning of death and beyond. This forms the subject matter of one of the Upanishads called Katha Upanishad or Kathopanishad.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: From which Upanishad, have the words “Satyameva Jayate” been taken ?
questions.explanation: The words “Satyameva Jayate’ is a Sanskrit word taken from the ‘Mundakopanishad'. The meaning of the word is “truth alone triumphs.” It was adopted as the national motto of India. It is inscribed in the script at the base of the national emblem. On January 26, 1950, it was adopted by the Government of India.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: King Asvapati of the Upanishadic period was the ruler of:
questions.explanation: The Upanishads state that some Kshatriya kings who were great scholars and philosophers also imparted knowledge to Brahmins. Some of them were- King Janak of Videha, King Pravahanjabali of Panchal, King Asvapati of Kekaya and King Ajatshatru of Kashi. Asvapati was a Kshatriya king. He was well known as a learned teacher of the age. The Kekaya kingdom was situated on the bank of river Beas, east of Gandhara kingdom. King Asvapati ruled Kekaya when Janak was the king of Videha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Vedic river Askini is identified with which one of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: Vedic river Askini is identified with a present-day river named as Chenab, also popularly known as Chandrabhaga. The river Chenab originates from Tandi in Lahul Spiti where two rivulets namely Chandra and Bhaga meet to form this river.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Fundamental or basic script of the ‘Rig Veda’ was –
questions.explanation: The basic script of the Rig Veda was Brahmi. The work on a script or ‘Bhasa’ is said to have been started by Brahma. For thousands of years, the script was known after him as the Brahmi script. The Rig Veda is divided into 10 Mandals, which consist of 1028 Sukta and 10552 Mantra. According to Patanjali, there are 21 branches of Rig Veda. The priests of Rig Veda were called ‘Hota'. * In the Vedic rituals HOTA is associated with the [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Mains) 2013] - Rig Veda

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: There is a similarity in Avesta and the Rig Veda, from which region the Avesta is related to –
questions.explanation: According to a definition given about the Aryans: The Indo-Iranian group whose members composed the Zoroastrian scriptures, the Avesta and the Hindu scriptures such as the Vedas, called themselves Aryans. So it is clear that in the Vedic period it was the region of present-day Iran, where Zoroastrianism prevailed, and the ‘Avesta’ was written by Zoroastrians.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The name 'Aghanya' mentioned in many passages of the Rig Veda refers to :
questions.explanation: It was the cow which was considered as “Aghanya” during Vedic period. “Aghanya” means not worthy of being killed. This status of the cow shows how pious it was considered during the Vedic period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the early Rigvedic period, what was considered to be the most valuable property?
questions.explanation: Cattle breeding was the most important economic activity of the Rigvedic people. Prayers were offered to increase the number of cattle. It was a medium of exchange. A cow is considered as a deity in some Suktas of Rig Veda.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following rivers mentioned in the Rig Veda indicates the relations of Aryans with Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: Rivers mentioned in the Rig Veda namely Kubha (Kabul), Kramu (Kurram), Gomti (Gomal) and Suvastu (Swat) were flowing through Afghanistan which indicates that there were deep relations of Aryans with the country. * The Vedic river Kubha was located in [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1999] - Afghanistan

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The ‘Mantra’ famous with the name of ‘Gayatri Mantra’ found in which of the following scriptures –
questions.explanation: The Gayatri Mantra was first written in Sanskrit in the Rig Veda by the Brahmarshi Vishwamitra. Its meaning is “May the Almighty God illuminate our intellect to lead us along the righteous path.”

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the List-I and List-II and choose the correct answer from the code given below: List-I List-II (Vedic Rivers) ( Modern Name) A. Kubha 1. Gandak B. Parushni 2. Kabul C. Sadaneera 3. Ravi D. Shutudri 4. Sutlej Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: Rivers given in the options are correctly matched as follows with their modern names – (Vedic Rivers) (Modern name) Kubha - Kabul Parushni - Ravi Sadaneera - Gandak Shutudri - Sutlej

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Vedic deities was believed to be their priest ?
questions.explanation: Brihaspati is also known as Deva-guru (teacher or priest of Gods), is the guru of the Devas (Gods).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: During the Rig Vedic period Nishka was an ornament of–
questions.explanation: During Rigvedic period, the gold necklace was called as ‘Nishka-Griva’ but later on word Nishka got associated with gold coins.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which officer was known as 'Bhagadugha' during Vedic administration?

options.a: Chief Officer of the Gambling Department

questions.explanation: Bhagadugha was associated with revenue administration in Vedic administration.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Boghaz-Koi is important because:

options.a: It was an important trading centre between Central Asia and Tibet
options.b: Inscriptions were found which mentioned the names of Vedic Gods and Goddesses
options.c: Original Texts of the Vedas were composed here

questions.answer_text: Inscriptions were found which mentioned the names of Vedic Gods and Goddesses
questions.explanation: Boghaz-Koi inscription (Asia Minor, Turkiye) is important because there is mention of four Vedic Gods, namely Indra, Varuna, Mitra and Nasatyas. * Which inscription tells about the Aryan’s movement from Iran to India? [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2009] - Boghaz-Koi * An inscription of 14th century B.C. which describes the Vedic Gods has been found in [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2016] - Boghaz-Koi

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following wrote on the original homeland of the Aryans?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak in his book ‘The Arctic Home in the Vedas’ propounded the theory that North Pole (Arctic region) was the original home of Aryans. But this theory of Tilak is not acceptable to historians.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The name of scripture in which ‘’Purusha Medha’ was mentioned is:
questions.explanation: ‘Purusha Medha’ has been mentioned in Shatpath Brahmana of Shukla Yajurveda and Taittiriya Brahmana of Krishna Yajurveda. No answer can be given all three are present in the given options. However many historians discuss Purushmedh Yojan while discussing Sathpath Brahmana only.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The priest associated with King Videgha Madhava referred in Shatapatha Brahmana was –
questions.explanation: It is believed that Saraswati was the scene of the activities of the famous Vedic tribes - the Bharatas, the Purus, and the Kurus. The Shatapatha Brahmana narrates the story of King Videgha Madhava (a king of Videha) accompanied by his priest Rishi Gautama Rahugana, carrying the sacred fire to east preserving thereby the tradition that the Kosalas and the Videhas received from their culture.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The word Gotra occurs for the first time in
questions.explanation: As a Rigvedic term, gotra simply means ‘cow shelter’ or ‘herd of cows’. The specific meaning “family, lineage kin” (as it were “herd within an enclosure”) is relatively more recent, first recorded around post-Vedic period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The famous battle of ‘Ten Kings’ as described in the Rig Veda was fought on the bank of
questions.explanation: There is an ancient story mentioned in the Rig Veda called the Dasharajnya or ‘Battle of 10 Kings’ on the bank of Parushni River. There lived a descendant of India’s eponymous king Bharata, named Sudas. The greatest achievement of Sudas was his thumping victory over a confederacy of ten kings.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following river among the following referred as ‘Matetama’, 'Devitama' and ‘Naditama’ in the Rig Veda.
questions.explanation: Saraswati River was considered as the most pious and respected river during the Rigvedic period. In the Rig Veda, Saraswati is referred as ‘Matetama,’ 'Devitama' and “Naditama’ means best of all mothers, best of all Goddesses and the best of all rivers respectively.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Give the name of the tribe which is not related to the ‘Panchjana’ of the Rig Veda Aryans:
questions.explanation: Pancha-Jana suggested five specific tribes whose eponymous ancestors were the founders of the clans, namely Yadu, Turvasa, Druhya, Anu and Puru. Kikat was not among them.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the ancient period chief-livelihood source of the Aryans was –
questions.explanation: In ancient time, the Aryans were dependent on Agriculture and hunting for their livelihood.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The word ‘Yava’ mentioned in Rig Veda is used for which agricultural product ?
questions.explanation: The word ‘Yava’ mentioned in Rig Veda is used for the food grain barley. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the Vedas, Sabha and Samiti are called as two daughters of Prajapati ?
questions.explanation: The clear distinction between Sabha and Samiti cannot be made but it is clear that ‘Sabha’ and ‘Samiti’ were clearly mentioned in the Atharva Veda as the two daughters of Prajapati.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Ayurveda’ that is ‘Science of Life’ appeared first in :
questions.explanation: ‘Ayurveda’ that is ‘Science of Life’ appeared first in Atharvaveda. Ayurveda is an Upaveda of Atharva Veda. It describes the thoughts and superstitions of common people. It comprises of various contents such as disease prevention, coordination, loyalty, marriage and love poetry.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the Rigvedic period, people believed mainly in –
questions.explanation: Sacrifice or Yajna was the central feature of Rigvedic religion. Domestic sacrifice was the general rule. Community sacrifices offered by kings were grand festivals. It was believed that Gods were pleased by Yajna or sacrifice.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Rig-vedic religion was–
questions.explanation: The most interesting aspect of Rig Vedic religion was its polytheistic character in which a number of Gods were worshipped. The Rig Vedic Aryans worshipped nature with intense feeling and endowed it with an animated soul. Vedic Gods were mainly classified into three groups- (1) God of sky-Varuna, Mitra, Surya, Vishnu, etc. (2) God of space- Indra, Rudra, etc. (3) God of the earth- Agni, Brihaspati, Soma, etc. Whenever these Vedic saints worship any God, they consider him to be the Supreme God, this is known as Ekaikyavaad. Other than this in Rigveda Ekeshwarvaad is supported by saying Ekam Satt Vipra bahudha badanti". Ekeshwarvaad of Rigveda included vision of Advaityavaad, Sarvadevtavaad and Bahudevatavaad. But the concept of one supreme God of Vedas is different from the modern Ishwarvaad.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The largest number of Rigvedic hymns are devoted to
questions.explanation: ‘Indra’ has been described as the most powerful deity in the Rig Veda. ‘Indra’ is the most important divinity in the Rig-Veda. A very large number of Rig Veda hymns (as many as 250 hymns) are devoted to him followed by ‘Agni’ (200 hymns). * Who is regarded as War-God in the Rig Veda? [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011] - Indra

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The largest number of the Hymns in Rig Veda belongs to–
questions.explanation: The largest number of hymns in Rigveda belongs to god Indra. But in the present question, in the absence of Indra we choose Agni (Second largest).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Study the following statements about the Vedic God Indra and select the correct answer from the codes given below: 1. Was the God of thunder. 2. Punished the sinners. 3. Was the guardian of the moral order. 4. Was the God of rain. Codes :
questions.explanation: In Vedas, Indra is the King and the Dev of Svarga (Heaven). He is the God of heaven, lightning, thunder and rains. Guardian of the Moral order (Rita) was lord Varuna. Some hymns, are prayers to God Indra for punishing the sinners, but in the absence of option 1, 2 and 4 we choose 1 and 4. * Who was the most popular God of the early Vedic Aryans? [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2008] - Indra

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: 800 B.C. to 600 B.C. is related to which era?
questions.explanation: 800 B.C. to 600 B.C. is related to Brahmana era. The period during seventh century B.C. or sixth century B.C. to third century B.C. is called as Sutra Period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Sarga, Pratisarga, Vansa, Manvantara and Vanshanucha-rita are the indicators of
questions.explanation: Puranas have five characteristics : Sarga, Pratisarga, Vansa, Manvantara and Vanshanucharita. Among these, Sarga and Pratisarga are the natural creation and renovation (cosmogony). Vansa means the history of Sage and God. Manvantara is meant for the period of different Manus and Vanshanucharit means the genealogy of kings.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The number of Puranas is–
questions.explanation: Puranas are the sacred literature of Hinduism. There are 18 Puranas namely, (1) Matsya Purana (2) Markandeya Purana (3) Bhagavat Puranam (4) Bhavishya Purana (5) Brahmanda Purana (6) Brahma Vaivrata Purana (7) Brahma Purana (8) Vamana Purana (9) Varaha Purana (10) Vishnu Purana (11) Vayu Purana (12) Agni Purana (13) Narada Purana (14) Padma Purana (15) Linga Purana (16) Garuda Purana (17) Skanda Purana (18) Kurma Purana. Out of these 18 Puranas, Srimad Bhagvatam is considered as the ‘Crown Jewel’ of all the Vedic literature.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Originally the Mahabharata was known as –
questions.explanation: Mahabharata originally had only 8,800 shlokas and its original name was ‘Jaya’ or Jayasamhita. Mahabharata today has 100,000 Shlokas and is believed to be written by Sage Veda Vyasa. * The Shatasahasri-Samhita is the nickname of which text? [U.P.B.E.O. (Pre.) 2019] - Mahabharata

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the post-Vedic period which was considered as the axis of Aryan Culture
questions.explanation: In the post-Vedic period, this region of Kuru, Panchala was considered the axis of Aryan culture because here great achievements happened in science, mathematics, astronomy, religion and philosophy.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The earliest evidence of the use of iron in India has been discovered from :
questions.explanation: Atranjikhera is a prehistoric and historic excavated archaeological site on the bank of Kali river, a tributary of Ganga. This site was first identified by Sir Alexander Cunningham in his survey report in 1861-62 but excavated by R.C. Gaur. A trial trench put in 1962 was followed in the next year by digging an a small scale. Regular excavation was started in 1964. The earliest evidence of iron used in the region dates back to around 1000 B.C.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists : List - I List - II A. Indus Valley 1. Pastoral Civilization B. Later Vedic Society 2. Land Lordism C. Rigvedic Society 3. Agrarian D. Medieval Period 4. Urban Codes : A B C D
questions.explanation: The correctly matched list is as follows : List - I List - II Indus Valley – Urban Civilization Later Vedic Society – Agrarian Rigvedic Society – Pastoral Medieval Period – Land Lordism

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the events of Buddha’s life is known as ‘Mahabhinishkramana’?
questions.explanation: Gautam Buddha, also known as Siddhartha (childhood name), was born in 563 B.C. in Shakya Kshatriya family in Lumbini near Kapilvastu (Nepal). His father’s name was Shuddhodana who was the chief of the Shakya clan. His mother was Mayadevi who was from the ‘Koliyan clan.’ At the age of 29, he left his home on his horse “Kantaka” accompanied by Channa and this was called as “Mahabhinishkramana”. He died at the age of 80 years in 483 B.C. at Kushinagar (the first capital city of Malla Kingdom) which is known as “Mahaparinirvana”. * Gautam Buddha’s mother was from which clan? [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2008] - Koliyan clan * Gautam Buddha was born at [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2002] - Lumbini

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: From which inscriptions of the following dynasty Lumbini was known as Buddha’s birthplace?
questions.explanation: From the Mauryan dynasty emperor Ashoka’s Rummindei Pillar inscription, it is known that Lumbini is the birthplace of Gautam Buddha. According to this inscription King Ashoka came here (Lumbini) in the 20th year of his coronation and worshipped the place where Shakya Muni was born. In ad-dition to that, he also exempted Lumbini from Bali tax and was asked to pay only an eighth share of the produce as it was the birthplace of Gautam Buddha. * Which one inscriptions of Ashoka confirms the tradition that Gautama Buddha was born in Lumbini ? [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Mains) 2010] - Rummindei Pillar Inscription * The Rummindei Pillar of Ashoka was up to mark? [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl.) (Mains) 2008] - Birth of Buddha * The Rummindei Pillar of Ashoka was put up to mark [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2008] – Birth of Buddha

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where did Mahatma Buddha’s ‘Mahaparinirvan’ take place?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Buddha delivered his first sermon at the site of Deer Park at Sarnath. Later he moved towards Kosala, Kap-ilavastu, Vaishali and Rajgriha to propagate the teachings of Buddhism. The king of Kosala Prasenjit with his entire family adopted discipleship of Buddha. During his campaign, he reached ‘Pava’, the capital of Mallas. At Pava, Buddha stayed in the mango grove of Chund, the blacksmith. There Chund provided him a large amount of Sukaramaddava, which resulted in sickness with the flow of blood and violent deadly pains, but Buddha reached Kushinara (Capital of Republic of Malla). Here he abandoned his body in 483 BC at the age of 80 years. It is also known as Mahaparinirvan. * Gautam Buddha attained “Mahaparinirvana” in kingdom of [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2011] - Malla

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Kushinagar was the capital of Malla Republic. Reason (R) : Lord Buddha’s Mahaparinirvana took place in Kushinagar. Select the correct answer using the code given below :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Kushinagar was the capital of Malla and also one of the sixteen Mahajanpadas of the 6th century B.C. Lord Buddha’s Mahaparinirvana took place in Kushinagar. Therefore both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Mahaparinirvana Temple is located at
questions.explanation: Mahaparinirvana temple is situated in Kushinagar district of Uttar Pradesh. It is very famous statue of Buddha. The image was unearthed during an excavation in 1876-77 A.D.. Carved from Chunar sandstone, the statue represents the dying Buddha reclining on his right side.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the last person to get enlightenment from Gautam Buddha ?
questions.explanation: Gautam Buddha, in his last years, went to his disciple named Chund at Pava, where he suffered food poisoning after eating Sukaramaddava offered by Chund. Then he went to Kushinagar (capital city of the Mallas Kingdom) where he gave his last sermon to “Subhaddha” and finally attained the “Mahaparin-irvana” at Kushinagar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where did Buddha reside during the last rainy season of his life?
questions.explanation: Buddha resided in Vaishali during the last rainy season of his life. Actually, Buddha reached Beluva which was in the suburb of Vaishali to spend his time during rainy season at the age of eighty years with his two disciples, one of them popularly known as ‘Ananda.’

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was Alara Kalama?
questions.explanation: Alara Kalama was one of the best and well known religious teacher. Ascetic Buddha went to study under him. He stayed and learnt many things, including meditation. He worked hard and eventually equalled his teacher in learning. Finally, Alara Kalama could not teach Buddha anymore, and he said, “You are the same as I am now. There is no difference between us. Stay here and take my place and teach my students with me.” Alara Kalama was an Acharya of Samkhya philosophy and was renowned for his spiritual strength.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: At which place did Mahatma Buddha give his ‘Dham-machakkhapavathana’?
questions.explanation: After his enlightenment in Bodhgaya, Buddha went to Sar-nath, where he delivered his first sermon which is known in Pali as the ‘Dhammachakkhapavathana’ or “Dharma Chakra Pravartana.” Sarnath is one of the four holy places associated with the life of Buddha. Other three important places related to Buddhism are Lumbini (birthplace of Buddha) Bodhgaya (the place of enlightenment of Buddha) and Kushinagar (place of death popularly known as Mahaparinirvana in Buddhism). * Who gave his first sermon in Sarnath [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1993] - Mahatma Buddha * In Buddhist text “Dharmachakra Parvartana” is known as [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004] - First Sermon at Sarnath

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which event of Buddha’s life is represented by the wheel with deer, in Indian Art ?
questions.explanation: First preaching event of Buddha’s life is represented by the wheel with deer in Indian art. Buddha delivered his first preaching in Mrigadava Sarnath.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List- I (Sign) with List II (Meaning) and select the correct answer using the codes given below. List-I (Sign) List –II (Meaning) A. Birth 1. Bodhi tree B. First Sermon 2. Dharma Chakra Pravartana C. Enlightenment 3. Horse D. Great- Departure 4. Lotus Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: The correctly matched list is as follows : List - I - List - II Birth - Lotus First Sermon - Dharma Chakra Pravartana Enlightenment - Bodhi Tree Great- Departure - Horse

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Gautam Buddha gave the maximum sermons at which place ?
questions.explanation: Most of the disciples of Gautama Buddha were from Kosala region. He delivered his maximum sermons at Shravasti, the capital of Kosala.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Buddha had visited Kaushambi during the reign of
questions.explanation: Mahatma Buddha visited Kaushambi during the reign of “King Udayana”. Under the influence of Pindola Bharadwaj, Udayan turned to Buddhism and donated Ghoshit Ram Vihar to Bhikshu Sangh.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: First Buddhist Conference after the death of Buddha was presided over by:
questions.explanation: The first Buddhist Council was held soon after the Maha-parinirvana of the Buddha, under the patronage of King Ajatashatru with the monk Mahakasapa presiding at Rajgriha, in the Saptaparni Cave. The idea was to preserve Buddha’s teachings (Sutta) and rules for disciples (Vinaya). Ananda, one of the great disciples of Buddha, recited Suttas and Upali; another disciple recited Vinaya. Abhidhamma Pitaka was also included. * The first Buddhist Council was held during the reign of [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2010] - Ajatashatru * The first Buddhist council was held in which city [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2000] - Rajgir * ‘Saptaparni Cave’ is situated in [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2014] - Rajgriha

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Four Buddhist Councils were held in the following places. Arrange them in chronological order by using the code given below : 1. Vaishali 2. Rajgriha 3. Kundalavana 4. Pataliputra Code :
questions.explanation: First Buddhist council was held soon after the death of Bud-dha under the patronage of King Ajatashatru with the monk Mahakassapa presiding at Saptaparni Cave at Rajgriha. The second council took place during the reign of Kalasoka 100 years after Buddha’s death in Vaishali and was presided over by Sabakami. The third council was held during the reign of Ashoka at Pataliputra, and the fourth council was held during the reign of Kanishka at Kashmir (Kundalavana). * Second Buddhist Council was held at which place? [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Mains)2014] - Vaishali * The Fourth Buddhist Council was held during the reign of [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Mains) 2013] - Kanishka

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following sources mention the occurrence of the third Buddhist Council during the reign of Ashoka: 1. Inscriptions of Ashoka 2. Dipavamsa 3. Mahavamsa 4. Divyavadana Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: According to Sinhalese folklore –“Dipavamsa” and “Mahavamsa”, the third Buddhist Council was held in “Pataliputra” during the reign of Ashoka. The chairperson of this Buddhist Council was Moggaliputta Tissa, the famous Buddhist mendicant.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct about Lord Buddha? 1. He was born in Kapilvastu. 2. He attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya. 3. He discarded the Vedic religion. 4. He preached noble truths Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, was born in 563 BC in Lumbini (now in Nepal) in Shakya Kshatriya clan of Kapilavastu. He believed in the theory of Karma. Buddha discarded Vedas and Vedic rituals. Instead, he believed in noble deeds and acts in place of Vedic rituals. He has given four noble truths often known as Arya Satya (1) Life means suffering (2) The origin of suffering is attachment (3) The cessation of suffering is attainable (4) There is a path to the cessation of suffering. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Buddhist sacred place is situ-ated on the Bank of River Niranjana.
questions.explanation: The Buddhist sacred place, Bodhgaya where Buddha got enlightenment, is situated on the bank of river Niranjana.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The teachings of Buddha are related to –
questions.explanation: The teachings of Mahatma Buddha are mainly based on the purity and holiness of conduct.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following wanted to become the leader of the Sangha even during the lifetime of Buddha?
questions.explanation: Devadatta, the cousin of Mahatma Buddha, in his early days, he was a follower of Buddha and a good monk as well. But later he tried to become the leader of Sangha in place of Buddha but did not succeed. From the beginning, he was thinking of becoming the leader of Sangha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is/are true about Gautam Buddha? 1. He believes in “Karma” 2. He believes in rebirth 3. Attaining Nirvana 4. Belief in the power of God Code :
questions.explanation: Mahatma Buddha believed in the doctrine of “Karma.” He used to believe in the concept of rebirth and attainment of Nirvana but did not believe in the existence of God and his power. Budha believes in rebirth. Previous life of Buddha is recorded in Jataka.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The entry of women as a “Bhikshuni” into the Buddhist Sangha was allowed by Gautam Buddha at –
questions.explanation: On the request of his disciple “Ananda”, Gautam Buddha allowed the entry of women as Bhikshuni into Buddhist Sangha at Vaishali. The first woman who was admitted into the Buddhist Sangha was Mahaprajapati Gautami.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is “Tripitaka”?

options.d: Collection of the preachings of Buddha

questions.answer_text: Collection of the preachings of Buddha
questions.explanation: Tripitaka is the most important holy book of Buddhism. It has been divided into three parts, namely, Sutta Pitaka – which consists of sermons and teachings of Buddha, Vinaya Pitaka – the collection of the rules governing the Sangha and monks and Abhidhamma Pitaka - which deals with the philosophy of Buddhism. * Which Buddhist text contains the rules of monastic life? [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1996] - Vinaya Pitaka

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What does ‘Triratna’ mean in Buddhism?
questions.explanation: Buddha, Dhamma and Sangh are three jewels (Triratna) of Buddhism. After the death of Buddha, his teachings were collected in three parts known as Tripitakas. The Tripitakas are Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka and Abhidhamma Pitaka.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ashokaram monastery was situated at –
questions.explanation: According to the famous Buddhist text mahavansh, the Mauryan ruler Ashoka built Ashokaram Vihar in Pataliputra under the supervision of a monk named Indragupta.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Stupa site which is not connected with any incident of Lord Buddha’s life, is :
questions.explanation: The Stupa at Bodhgaya is related to the enlightenment of Buddha. Sarnath is related to Dharma Chakra Pravartana and Kushinagar or Kusinara is related to the death of Bud-dha while Sanchi Stupa is not related to any incident of Buddha’s life.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which is the correct chronological order of the follow-ing stupas?
questions.explanation: Bharhut and Sanchi stupas were constructed during the reign of Mauryan emperor Ashoka. Some historical sources also consider that Dhamekh stupa was built during the reign of Ashoka. Amravati stupa was built during the period of Sat-vahanas. It is not possible to decide the chronological order of the construction of Bharhut, Sanchi and Dhamekh stupa. This question should be excluded from evaluation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is considered the best Stupa ?
questions.explanation: From the perspective of architecture, the Stupa of Sanchi is considered as the best. Sanchi is located in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh. This stupa was built by Ashoka. It is famous across the world for its stupas, monasteries, temples and pillars, which date back to the 3rd century B.C. Thus option (c) is the right answer. The stupa of Bharhut is situated in Satna district of Madhya Pradesh. Bharhut stupa was discovered by Alexander Cunningham. Amravati Stupa is located on the right bank of Krishna river in the Palnadu district of Andhra Pradesh. Colin Mackenzie traced this Stupa in 1797 A.D. Dhamekh Stupa of Sarnath (Varanasi) was built during the time of Ashoka, whose present form was built during the Gupta period. This stupa is designed on the flat surface without raising the base. * Which ruler constructed the ‘Sanchi Stupa’? [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1991] - Ashoka

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: “World is unstable and transient “ is related to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Impermanence also called Anitya, is one of the essential doctrines and a part of three marks of existence in Buddhism. The doctrine asserts that all of the conditioned existence, without exception, is transient, evanescent and inconstant. All temporal things, whether material or mental, are compounded objects in a continuous change of condition subject to decline and destruction.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following is known as the ‘Light of Asia’?
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha, also known as Siddhartha, Gautama, Shakyamuni or simply the Buddha, was a sage on whose teachings Buddhism was founded. Buddha is also prominently known as the ‘Light of Asia’ or the Light Beam. Edwin Arnold wrote a book “ the Light of Asia” based on the life of Buddha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: 'Milindpanha' is in the form of a dialogue between King Milind and Buddhist Saint. The concerned saint was –
questions.explanation: Milindpanha is in the form of a dialogue between King Milind and Buddhist Saint Nagasena.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Sir Edwin Arnold book ‘The Light of Asia’ is based on–
questions.explanation: The 'Light of Asia' subtitled 'The Great Renunciation' is a book by Sir Edwin Arnold. The first edition of the book was published in July 1879. This book is based upon the contents of ‘Lalit Vistara’.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between Hinayana and Mahayana sects of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: The fundamental difference between Hinayana and Ma-hayana sects of Buddhism is regarding treating Buddha as God. Hinayana believes in Buddha as a great man, whereas Mahayana started worshipping Buddha through idols treat-ing him as God.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following laid the foundation of idol wor-ship in the country?
questions.explanation: In context of the following, Buddhism laid the foundation of idol worship in the country. The followers of Mahayana primarily started worshipping the idols of Buddha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The standing statue of Gautam Buddha was built in which period?
questions.explanation: In India, the Gandhara art flourished during the Kushana rule. Particularly Kanishka, the greatest of the Kushanas was a great patron of art and architecture. It was during his reign that Gandhara school of art flourished. Both sitting and standing postures of Buddha’s statues were carved out in the Mathura school. The Kushana art of Gandhara is mainly known for the wealth of sculptures recovered from the numerous Buddhist stupas and monasteries.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Sarnath Buddha image of Bhumisparsha Mudra belongs to –
questions.explanation: The Bhumisparsha Mudra of Gautama Buddha at Sarnath be-longs to the Gupta period. This mudra represents steadfastness. The “Dhyani Buddha Akshobhya” also is associated with the earth witness mudra because he was immovable in keeping a vow never to feel anger or disgust at others. The mudra also symbolizes the union of skilful means (upaya), symbolized by the right hand touching the earth and wisdom (prajna), symbolized by the left hand on the lap in a meditation posture.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The largest and the most evolved rock-cut Chaitya hall of the Hinayana phase is situated at :
questions.explanation: The Chaitya is the largest and most evolved cave temples of the Hinayana phase of Buddhism, situated at Karle in Pune district of Maharashtra.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following rock cut caves eleven headed Bodhisattava image is depicted?
questions.explanation: The Kanheri caves located in Salsette Island are a major tourist destination of the city of Mumbai in Maharashtra. These caves are located in the Sanjay Gandhi National Park complex. Kanheri mentioned in ancient records as Kanhashail, Krishnagiri, Kanhagiri, was the main center of Buddhists. It has the largest number of caves built at a single hill. Kanheri caves were built in the first century B.C. and they were in use till 11th century AD. Cave number 41 (earlier it was numbered 23) houses an interesting idol of Avalokiteshvara with four arms and eleven heads. It is the only statue of its kind in India. The worship of this form of Bodhisattva was prevalent in China, Chinese Turkistan, Cambodia and Japan in 7th-8th CE.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Vallabhi University was situated in –
questions.explanation: Vallabhi, one of the most important centres of Buddhist learn-ing, was situated in Gujarat. It is also known as Vallabhipura and was the capital of ancient Maitraka dynasty.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Lord Buddha preached the following four noble truths. Put them in correct order using the codes given below : A. There is suffering. B. There is a cessation of suffering. C. There is a path leading to the cessation of suffering. D. There is the cause of suffering. Code :
questions.explanation: After attaining enlightenment, to preach his thoughts, Gautama Buddha arrived at Rishipattan (Sarnath), where he delivered his sermon to five Brahmans. It is also known as Dharmachakra Pravartana. The sermon was related to sufferings, the cause of suffering and its solution. The concept of eight-fold path forms the theme of ‘Dharma Chakra Pravartana Sutta’ which means sermon of the turning of the wheel of law. He prescribed ‘Noble Eightfold Path’ and ‘Four Noble Truths’ which were accepted as basic tenets by all Buddhist sects. The four noble truths in chronological order are as follows-i. There is suffering. ii. There is the cause of suffering. iii. There is a cessation of suffering. iv. There is a path leading to the cessation of suffering.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Both Jainism and Buddhism believe that:

options.a: Philosophy of karma and transmigration of soul were correct
options.b: Salvation could be possible only after death
options.c: Both men and women could attain salvation
options.d: Middle course of life was the best one

questions.answer_text: Philosophy of karma and transmigration of soul were correct
questions.explanation: Both Buddhism and Jainism believe in the concept of Karma, which states that our past actions affect our present and future life. One could do evil in this life and be reborn as a worm in the next life. Similarly, afflictions in this life are often explained away as the effects of Karma of a previous life (or from misdeeds earlier in this life). Both of them believe in the philosophy of Karma and rebirth.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: According to philosophy of Buddhism : Assertion (A) : Rejected the concept of Rebirth. Reason (R) : Soul is mortal. Choose the correct option:

options.a: (A) and (R) both are true, and (R) is the proper explanation of (A).
options.b: (A) and (R) both are true, and (R) is not the proper explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Pratiyasamutpada is the essence of Buddhist teachings. The invincibility of Vedas and immortalization of soul propounded by Brahmin Granthas was inadmissible in Buddhism. Even though they rejected the immortalization theory of soul, they accepted the principle of rebirth and theory of Karma. According to them, life originates due to the causes of various preconditions that are interdependent. One type of state comes into being as a result of another previous state. So it is clear that Assertion (A) is not correct, but Reason (R) is correct.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Doctrine of void (Shunyata) was propounded by the Buddhist philosopher :
questions.explanation: Nagarjuna’s primary contribution to Buddhist philosophy was the use of the concept of Sunyata or doctrine of void. The famous literary work “Madhyamikakarika” provides one of Nagarjuna’s most famous quotations on emptiness or co-arising.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct about Buddhism? 1. It did not reject caste and class. 2. It challenged highest social ranked Brahmins. 3. It pointed certain castes as low. Choose the correct answer from the code given below. Code :
questions.explanation: Although Buddhism had accepted the caste system up to some extent but they challenged the social rank of Brahmins who were at the top during that period. In Buddhism, some of the castes were placed as low.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The reasons included in the expansion of Buddhism– 1. The simplicity of religion 2. Special appeal towards Dalits 3. Missionary concept of religion 4. Regional language 5. The soundness of Vedic spirit by Philosophers– Code :
questions.explanation: The main reason for the spread of Buddhism was its simplicity. Its eight-fold path known as ‘Arya-Satya’ and concept of non-violence were simple and understandable by the common people. Buddha spread his message in the simple language or the language of common people. Buddhism did not believe in caste-distinctions. The non-Brahmins, particularly Dalits were attracted by the simplicity of Buddhism. They also followed the missionary concept.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements, what is the difference between chaityas and viharas.

options.a: Viharas is a place of worship while chaitya is dwelling place of the Buddhist monks.
options.b: Chaitya is a place of worship while Vihar is a dwelling place.
options.c: There is no particular difference between both of them.
options.d: Viharas and Chaityas both are used as dwelling place.

questions.answer_text: Chaitya is a place of worship while Vihar is a dwelling place.
questions.explanation: A Chaitya-Griha Buddhist cave is a meeting or assembly chamber that is often used for prayer, while Viharas are the shelter accommodations of the monks during the rainy season.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Karmapa Lama belongs to which of the following sects of Tibetan Buddhism?
questions.explanation: Karmapa Lama belongs to the Kangyupa sect of Tibetan Buddhism.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The originator of the Jain religion is –
questions.explanation: First Tirthankara Rishabhdev or Aadinath is known as the originator of Jain religion. Mahavira Swami was 24th Tirthankar of Jain religion, who propagated the Jain philosophy during 6th Century B.C.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Parshvanatha, the Jain ‘Tirthankara’ was associated mainly with which of the following places?
questions.explanation: Lord Parshvanath was 23rd Tirthankara of Jain Religion. He was born in Varanasi, was the son of King Aswasena and Queen Vama of Varanasi. He obtained Kaivalya (complete knowledge) in Ashrampad Udyan near Varanasi and he attained Parinirvan on the Mount Sammed Shikhar or Sammeta.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following place is known as a place of Pilgrimage because of being related to Parshvanath?
questions.explanation: Parshvanatha was the 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism. Parshvanatha was born to King Asvasena and Queen Vama of Varanasi in 850 BC. He belonged to the Ikshvaku dynasty. He lived as the formal prince of Varanasi and at the age of thirty, he renounced the world to become a monk. He meditated for 84 days before attaining Kevala Jnana. He achieved Parinirvana at Sammed Shikhar that’s why this place is also known as a place of pilgrimage for Jains.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below: List-I List-II (Tirthankara) (Cognizance) A. Adinatha 1. Bull B. Mallinatha 2. Horse C. Parshvanatha 3. Snake D. Sambhavnatha 4. Water Jar Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: The correctly matched list is as follows – (Tirthankaras) (Cognizance) Adinatha - Bull Mallinatha - Water Jar Parshvanatha - Snake Sambhavnatha - Horse

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched? (Tirthankar) - (Nirvan Place)
questions.explanation: Vasupujya was the 12th Tirthankar of Jainism. He attained Nirvana or Moksha in Champapur (Bihar). All other pairs are correctly matched.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following 'Tirthankara' and arrange them in chronological order: I. Abhinandan II. Vimal Nath III.Munishubratha Nath IV. Padmaprabhu Select the correct answer from the code given below. Code :
questions.explanation: Abhinandana Natha was 4th Tirthankara, Padmaprabhu was 6th Tirthankara, Vimal Nath was 13th and Munishubratha Nath was 20th Tirthankara. * The word Tirthankara is related to [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1993] - Jains

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following was not a Jain Tirthankara ?
questions.explanation: The term Tirthankara is related to Jain Religion. It is known that there were 24 Tirthankara who contributed to Jain religion and who propagated Jain philosophy from time to time. These are - (1) Rishabhnath (2) Ajitnath, (3) Sambhavnath, (4) Abhinandannath, (5) Sumatinath, (6) Padmaprabha, (7) Suparshvanath, (8) Chandraprabha, (9) Suvidhinatha, (10) Sheetalanath (11) Shreyanshnath, (12) Vasupujya (13) Vimalnath (14) Anantnath (15) Dharmnath (16) Shantinath, (17) Kunthunath, (18) Aranath, (19) Mallinath, (20) Munisuvrata, (21) Naminatha, (22) Arishtnemi, (23) Parshvanath, (24) Mahavira Swami.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Prabhasgiri is a pilgrim spot of :
