questions.explanation: Prabhasgiri is a Jain pilgrimage site located in Kaushambi, U.P. The site Prabhasgiri is related to 6th Jain Tirthankar, Padmaprabha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists : List-I List-II (Place) (Related Tirthankar) A. Shravasti 1. Rishabhanath B. Kakandi 2. Padmaprabhu C. Ayodhya 3. Suvidhanath D. Pabhosa 4. Sambhavnath Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct match is as follows : List-I List-II (Place) (Related Tirthankar) Shravasti Sambhavnath Kakandi Suvidhanath (Pushpdant) Ayodhya Rishabhanath Pabhosa Padmaprabhu

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Kundalpur is the birthplace of –
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami was born in Kundagram (Kundalpur) near Vaishali in approx 599 BC. His mother Trishala was the sister of Chetak, the head of Lichchhavi republic, and father Siddhartha was the head of Gyatrik Kshatriya. Nandivardhan was his elder brother.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: On the banks of which river did Mahavira Swami attain enlightenment?
questions.explanation: Mahavir Swami attained enlightenment at the bank of river Rijupalika in the village of Jrimbhik.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the first follower of Mahavira?
questions.explanation: Among the early visitors to Mahavira during his wandering was Jamali, his son-in- law. Jamali met Mahavira while the latter was in Kshatriya- Kundagram, the village where Mahavira was born. He took the vow together with five hundred of the warrior caste. Jamali was the first disciple of Lord Mahavira.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The doctrine of three jewels-Right faith, Right action and Right Knowledge, is the crowning glory of :
questions.explanation: Three means are said to be important for ‘Moksha’ in Jain philosophy: Right faith, Right action and Right knowledge. These are known as ‘Triratna’ in Jain religion. Freedom from the bondage and effect of evil omens is called Sanvar Tattva to make the spirit free from the bondage of all. The destruction of Karma is the Nirjara element.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following religions does not trust in the concept of ‘final annihilation of the world’?
questions.explanation: As per Jainism, the Universe and all its substances are eternal. There is no concept of 'final annihilation of the world'.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Basic point of Jainism is-
questions.explanation: Jainism is also known as the religion of Ahimsa (non-violence). Ahimsa supersedes all concepts, ideologies, rules, customs and practices. Ahimsa, Anekantvad and Aparigraha are the cardinal principles of Jainism.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which one of the following languages was the earliest Jain literature compiled?
questions.explanation: All the initial religious Jain literature has been written in the Ardha-Magadhi. Its twelve Angas are in ‘Ardha-Magadhi.’ These holy books were finally compiled in the sixth century A.D. at Vallabhi near Gujarat.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Svetambara Agama was finally edited at the Jain Council of –
questions.explanation: In the reign of Chandragupta Maurya, 1st Jain Council was held in which Shwetambara Agama were edited. Since all the ancient Jain text got destroyed, so to recompile them another Jain council was organised in 4th century BC in which followers of Bhadrabahu did not participate.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Yapaniya was the sect of-
questions.explanation: Yapaniya was a sect of Jain religion; which is believed to have originated from Digambaras. However, they also used to follow certain Shwetambar opinions. The Yapaniyas worshipped nude images of the Tirthankaras in their temples.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Ajivaka’ sect was founded by:
questions.explanation: Makkhali Gosala was a disciple of Mahavira in the early period, later fell out with Mahavira due to the difference of opinion with him and founded an independent creed “Ajivaka.” Although, various sources mention Ajivika scholars like Nanda, Vaccha and Kisa samkicca even before Makkhali Gosala, he is attributed to popularising the sect for first time. The belief of the sect is known as ‘Niyatiwad’ according to which every matter in the world is being controlled and operated by destiny (fate). * Who rendered that “Fate assigns everything, human is incapable.” [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2006] Aajivakas

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below : List-I List-II (Acharya) (Doctrine) A. Lakulisa 1. Ajivaka B. Nagarjuna 2. Sunyavada C. Bhadrabahu 3. Pasupat D. Gosala 4. Jain Codes : A B C D
questions.explanation: The correctly matched list is as follows - List-I List-II (Acharya) (Doctrine) Lakulisa Pasupat Nagarjuna Sunyavada Bhadrabahu Jain Gosala Ajivaka

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The famous pilgrimage of Buddhists as well as of Jains in Uttar Pradesh is at
questions.explanation: The present Kaushambi district, carved out of Prayagraj on 4th April 1997, is located 55 km away from the south-west of Prayagraj. Kaushambi has been mentioned several times in Vedic and Jain literature. According to Puranas, Nicakshu, the sixth in line from Parikshita, transferred his capital from Hastinapur to Kaushambi as Hastinapur was ravaged by floods, invasion of locusts and upheavals in the Kuru family itself. According to Jain texts, Kushambi was named due to an excess of Kushamb trees in the town. It is the famous pilgrimage site of Jains and Buddhists. Mahatma Buddha preached many times in this city and made a number of disciples here. There were many monasteries found here, but the most famous among them was Ghoshitram monastery, which was built by Shresthi Ghoshit.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who built “Gommateshwara” statue at Sravanabelagola?
questions.explanation: It was built by Chamundraya who was a minister in the kingdom of Ganga ruler Rachmalla-IV (Panchmalla), approximately in 981 A.D.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List – I with List – II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists. List – I (God) List – II (Symbol) A. Shiva 1. Chakra B. Vishnu 2. Trident C. Ganesh 3. Veena D. Saraswati 4. Rope or noose Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: Correct match is as follows — List – I (God) List – II (Symbol) Shiva Trident Vishnu Chakra Ganesh Rope or noose Saraswati Veena

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ardhanarisvara, a figure of half Shiva and half Parvati, represents :

options.c: Union of God with his Shakti

questions.answer_text: Union of God with his Shakti
questions.explanation: Ardhanarishvara is a composite androgynous form of the Hindu God Shiva and his consort Parvati. Ardhanarishvara is depicted as half male and half female, split down the middle. The right half is usually the male Shiva, illustrating his traditional attributes. Ardhanarishvara represents the synthesis of masculine and feminine energies of the universe and illustrates how Shakti, the female principle of God, is inseparable from Shiva, the male principle of God.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who were Nayanars?
questions.explanation: In the medieval period, the devotional spirit was mainly spread in South India, especially in Tamil regions. There were two major sects behind the development of devotional spirit in the Tamil regions. The devotees worshipping God Vishnu were called Alvar and the devotees worshipping God Shiva were called Nayanara. They told that the personal love and dedication towards God is the only way to Moksha and opposed the caste system and its rigidity.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was not an ‘Alvar Saint’?
questions.explanation: Poigai, Pudam and Thirumangai were Alvar Saints, while Tirugyan was not an Alvar saint.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who were the first to worship Vasudeva Krishna :
questions.explanation: Under the Bhagavata religion, the initial form of Vaishnavism is shown in the worship of Lord Krishna, the son of Devaki. The initial name of Krishna was prevalent in the Panini age. The worshippers of Vasudev were known as Vasudevak (Bhagavata) in that age. According to Indian belief, Lord Krishna is considered as a supreme personality and has been worshipped since ancient ages.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following deities is represented in art as holding the plough ?
questions.explanation: According to the Indian cultural traditions, Balaram, the brother of Krishna is shown as holding plough in his arms. He is also known by the name of Haldhar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The number of forms of bhakti in the Bhagwata cult is–
questions.explanation: The Navadha (9) Bhakti (forms of Bhakti) has been recognised for acquiring Moksha in the Bhagavata cult. Thus, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The earliest archival evidence related to Bhagavat Religion is-
questions.explanation: The Garuda Pillar of Vidisha (Besanagar) is the first stone monument related to Bhagavata religion. This shows that the Yavana ambassador of Takshila (Taxila) accepted the Bhagavata religion and worshipped it after its establishment. Heliodorus is stated as ‘Bhagavata’ and Vasudeva is stated as ‘Devadevas’ (‘God of Gods’) in the article inscribed on it. * Heliodorus of ‘Besanagar inscription’ was a resident of [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2010] - Takshila (Taxila)

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which incarnation of Vishnu is depicted as saving the Earth from the Sea?
questions.explanation: Lord Vishnu took the form of Varaha to kill the king of Giants, Hiranyaksha and released the Earth from his clutch. In the pictures of the Purana, God Varaha has been shown balancing the earth on his teeth and arising from the sea. In this incarnation, the head of Varaha is on the human body having four arms holding Shankha, Chakra, Gada and Padma in his hands like God Vishnu fighting with demon Hiranyaksha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is the distinctive feature of a nastika and astika system in India ?

options.a: Belief in the existence of God
options.b: Belief in the doctrine of re-birth
options.c: Belief in the authenticity of the Vedas
options.d: Belief in the existence of heaven and hell

questions.answer_text: Belief in the authenticity of the Vedas
questions.explanation: In the context of 6th century BC, Astika sect belonged to those who believed in the authenticity of Vedas and Nastika sect was of those who did not believe in the authenticity of Vedas. Thus, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following gives equal importance to Jnana, Karma and Bhakti as a means of liberation?
questions.explanation: Jnana, Karma and Bhakti have the equal importance in Gita. Both Vedanta and Vishistadvaita Vedanta give supremacy to Bhakti (devotion toward God). Mimamsa has only propounded the Karma.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is not included in ‘Prasthan trayi’ ?
questions.explanation: Upanishad, Brahmasutra and Bhagavad Gita are said to be the ‘Prasthantrayi’ of Vedanta because these are the major epics of Vedanta. Among them, the Upanishad is the Prime Prasthan and the remaining two are known to be based on it. Shankaracharya is the oldest among all of Vedanta Acharyas who established their Vedanta sects by writing the commentary on ‘Brahmasutra.’

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The ancient place where the narration of entire Mahabharata was read in the conference of 60,000 hermits –
questions.explanation: Naimisharanya in Sitapur district of U.P. is considered to be the residence of 60,000 hermits. Here, Sut Goswami narrated the entire Mahabharata in front of Saunak and other hermits, when he was accomplishing the Yagya. Earlier, Vaisampayana narrated the story of Mahabharata for King Janamejaya.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Kand of Ramayana describes the first meeting of Rama and Hanumana?
questions.explanation: Valmiki was the author of Ramayana. There are total of seven Kands in this Adi Kavya written in Sanskrit. The fourth Kand of this Kavya is Kishkindha Kand in which the meeting of Rama and Hanuman, death of Bali and Sugriva becoming the king of Vanara is described.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Kumbh Mela at Nasik is held on which of the following river bank?
questions.explanation: The Kumbha Mela is held on the bank of Godavari river at an interval of every twelve years. It is also held on the bank of Ganga at Haridwar, on the confluence place of the Ganga and Yamuna (and extinct Saraswati) at Prayag (Prayagraj), on the bank of River Kshipra (Shipra) at Ujjain.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The earliest extant coins of India were of –
questions.explanation: Aahat coins or Punch marked coins were the earliest extant coins in India made up of silver. The marks on them were made by the stamp, so they are called as Aahat coins or Punch marked coins.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Buddha text has described 16 Mahajanpadas of 6th century B.C.?
questions.explanation: The 16 Mahajanapadas of 6th century B.C. were mentioned in Buddhist text ‘Anguttara Nikaya’. They were as follows-Anga, Magadha, Kashi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchal, Matsya, Surasen, Ashmaka, Avanti, Gandhara and Kamboj. The list of 16 Mahajanapadas also finds mention in Jain text Bhagavati Sutra.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: How many Mahajanapadas were located in present day of Uttar Pradesh among the oldest sixteen Mahajanapadas of India?
questions.explanation: Out of 16 Mahajanapadas, 8 were present in modern Uttar Pradesh. Kuru – Meerut, Delhi and Thaneshwar Panchala - Bareilly, Badaun, Farrukhabad Shurasena – Brajmandal areas Vatsa – Prayagraj and Kaushambi Koshal – Awadh area Malla – Deoria, Kushinagar etc. Kashi – Varanasi Chedi – Eastern Bundelkhand area

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one was not in the earlier Republic?
questions.explanation: The evidence of the existence of lots of republics is found during the Buddha period. They were as follows - (1) Shakya of Kapilavastu, (2) Bhagga of Sumsumagiri, (3) Buli of Alakappa, (4) Kalam of Kesaputta, (5) Koliya of Ramgama, (6) Malla of Kusinara, (7) Malla of Pava, (8) Moriya of Pippalivan, (9) Lichchhavi of Vaishali and (10) Videha of Mithila. Yaudheya was not in the earlier republic.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists: List-I List-II (King) (State) A.Pradyot 1. Magadha B.Udyan 2. Vatsa C.Prasenjit 3. Avanti D.Ajatshatru 4. Kosala Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: The Pali scriptures reveal that Pradyot was the king of Avanti. Udayana was the king of Vatsa Mahajanpada. Prasenjit was of Kosal and Ajatshatru was the king of Magadha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the ancient name of Ujjain?
questions.explanation: Ujjain, located in Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, is considered as the ancient historical town of India. This was one of the two capitals of Avanti which was one among the 16 Mahajanapadas. It is also known as Avantika.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Legend of Udayan-Vasavadatta is related to-
questions.explanation: The legend of Udayan-Vasavadatta is related to Ujjain. Great poet Bhaas has described this story in his drama ‘Svapnavasvadattam’, the love story of Vatsa king Udayan and Vasvadatta, the daughter of Avanti King Pradyot. The story is set during the time when Udayan was imprisoned in Ujjayini.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Matsya Mahajanapada of 6th Century B.C. was located in:
questions.explanation: Matsya Mahajanapad (6th century B.C.) was situated around areas of Jaipur, Alwar and Bharatpur in Rajasthan. Its capital was Viratnagar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History

questions.question: Who among the following made Varanasi his second capital?
questions.explanation: In 6th century BC Varanasi was the capital of Kashi Mahajanapada. It was received as dowry by Haryanka dynasty king Bimbisara when he married Mahakoshala, the sister of Koshala king Prasenjit. During the period of Ajatashatru, Prasenjit married his daughter Vajira to him and accepted his suzerainty over Kashi. Later on when Shishunag made Vaishali his capital, he appointed his son as deputy-king of Varanasi. Hence, it is not very clear from given options that who made Varanasi his second capital. However U.P.P.S.C. has accepted Shishunag as correct option.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies

questions.question: Which inscription is the evidence of King Nand?
questions.explanation: Kharvel was the most important emperor of Chedi dynasty of Kalinga. His Hathigumpha inscription is the major source of information about his reign. The engraving of canals in Kalinga by King Mahapadmananda is encrypted in this inscription. It is also the first inscription which tells about the engraving of canals. It mentions the donation of villages to Jain monks. This inscription also mentions that Kharvel defeated the three states Chola, Chera, and Pandyas of the south. Thus, option (a) is the correct answer. * The epigraphical evidence reveals that under the instructions of a Nanda king, a canal was dug in [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1999] - Kalinga

questions.explanation: The first three reasons given behind the success of Alexander in India are correct. Dr. Hemachandra Rai Chaudhary had mentioned 28 independent powers of that time. questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya is considered one of the greatest emperors of India. He was the first emperor who brought together the small fragmented kingdoms of the country and combined them into a single large empire. He expanded his empire to the edge of what is now known as Iran. He was the one who first unified India politically.

questions.question: Kautilya was prime minister of –
questions.explanation: Kautilya made an unforgettable contribution to the estab-lishment of Mauryan dynasty. He was well known as ‘Vishnugupta’ and ‘Chanakya.’ When Chandragupta Maurya had the responsibility of united Indian empire as emperor, Kautilya served as prime minister, advisor and chief priest. He was the pioneer scholar of political science and also known for his famous book ‘’Arthashastra”. This is one of the oldest books which is based on the political condition of India.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: By which name was Chanakya known in his childhood ?
questions.explanation: Sage Chanak gave his son the name Chanakya. The ancient Arthashastra has been traditionally attributed to Chanakya by a number of scholars. Arthashastra identifies its author by the name of Kautilya, except for one verse that refers to him by the name of Vishnugupta. In the question, the name of Chanakya in childhood is asked, so, from the above-options Vishnugupta is found to be the most appropriate answer. According to researcher Trobman, Chanakya or Kautilya is presumably the name of the author’s gotra (clan).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Arthashastra of Kautilya is a
questions.explanation: Arthashastra by Kautilya is the treatise on polity during the Mauryan monarch/kingdom. The Saptang theory of the state was introduced in it, which includes the seven elements of the state, these are – The King (Swami), Minister (Amatya), Territory (Janpada), Fort (Durg), Treasury (Kosa), Army (Danda) and Allies (Mitra). Arthashastra gives a detailed description about the then administration and agrarian system.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is the seventh part of the State according to Saptang Theory of State?
questions.explanation: According to Saptang Theory of State, Mitra (Ally) is the seventh part of the state ; Ally is like the ear of the state. Allies of King assist him in peace and war. In this context, Kautilya differentiates between idealistic and fake allies. Natural is better than artificial. Any King, whose friend is greedy, prurient and coward, ruin is inevitable.

The unified Mauryan empire extended from Bengal and Assam in the east to modern-day Afghanistan in the west, to Kashmir in the north and the Deccan plateau in the south.

Megasthenes does not mention slavery in India. According to him, no one could marry outside his caste, and no one could take to an occupation from the one fixed for his caste according to the varna system. * The division of Mauryan ‘Society into seven classes' is particularly mentioned in [U.P. questions.subject: History
questions.question: The earliest inscription on stone was in which language?
questions.explanation: Ashokan inscriptions describe the history of Ashoka properly. The inscriptions can be divided into three classes; (1) Rock inscription / petrograph (2) Column inscription (3) Cave inscription. Rock inscription is the group of 14 various inscriptions which were found at different places – Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra, Kalsi, Girnar, Dhauli, Jaugada, Yerraguddi and Sopara. Most of the inscription of Ashoka are written in Prakrit language and Brahmi script, only two inscriptions, Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra’s are in Kharosthi script. One ruined inscription, written in Aramaic script, was found from Taxila. Shar-i-Kuna (Kandhar Inscription) is in the bilingual (Greek-Aramaic) script while one Aramaic script of Ashokan inscription was obtained from Laghman.

questions.explanation: Major Rock Edict II: This rock edict, describes South Indian Kingdoms of Chodas (Cholas), Pandyas, Satiyaputtra, Keralputtra as well as the Tamraparni and Yavana king named Antiyoka and also the kings who were the neighbours of the Antiyaka. It also mentions providing medical treatment for humans and animals. Major Rock Edict XI: It explains the policy of dhamma and also emphasises on the individuals attitude towards elders and also abstaining from killing animals and being generous towards friends. Rock Edict XII: It directed and made requests for tolerance among different religious sects. Major Rock Edict XIII: This rock edict says the way of conquest is dhamma not war. questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Ashoka annexed Kalinga to the Mauryan Empire. Reason (R) : Kalinga controlled the land and sea routes to South India. Select the correct answer using the codes given below: Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The reasons which prompted Ashoka to invade Kalinga were both political and economical. The territory of Kalinga was like a bridge between north and south. People of Kalinga dominated the Indian Ocean and controlled the overseas trade. Their supremacy on the eastern sea coast virtually closed the sea routes in the east for the Magadhan merchants. Similarly, the land routes for internal trade from the Gangetic valley toward Deccan were also controlled by Kalinga. If the Kalinga were independent, the overseas and land trades of Magadha would be affected. That is why it was necessary to invade Kalinga for Mauryan dynasty. So, both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct, and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

Therefore, the first statement is correct. Ashoka appointed Dhamma-Mahamatras in the 14th year of his reign to promote his social and moral code (Dhamma, which included ethical and religious conduct). Hence, the second statement is also correct.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: India’s first hospital and herbal gardens were built by ?
questions.explanation: Ashoka built the first hospital and herbal garden in India. He founded hospitals, public gardens, and gardens for the growing of medicinal herbs. He also organized digging of wells and planting of trees for shade and created a ministry for the care of the aborigines and subject races of India.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A) : The Mauryan kings did not bestow land-grants on religious basis. Reason (R) : The peasants revolted against land grants. Select the correct answer using the codes given below : Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: The earliest epigraphic record of land grants on the basis of religion in India is found in the inscription of Satavahana. Mauryan emperors did not grant any land on religious basis. There is no description found about peasant revolt against land grants. Thus, Assertion (A) is right, while Reason (R) is wrong.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct about Mauryan Kings? They developed – A. Culture, Art and Literature B. Gold coins C. Provincial Division D. Kingship to Hindukush Code :
questions.explanation: Mauryan emperors played a major role in the development of culture, art and literature. Chandragupta’s empire spread over from Iran in the north-west to present north Karnataka in the south. According to historian Smith, Hindukush mountains was the strategic frontier of India. There were five provinces described in inscriptions of Ashoka i.e. (1) Uttarapath (2) Avantiratha (3) Kalinga (4) Dakshinapath (5) Prachyapatha. Regularization of gold coins in India is credited to Indo-Greek kings. Hence A, C, D are correct about Mauryan emperors.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Bhaga’ and ‘Bali’ were:
questions.explanation: “Bhaga” and “Bali” were the sources of revenue in ancient India. According to Arthashastra, King was the owner of the land. He had a share in produce from the land. This tax was known as ‘Bhaga’ whereas ‘Bali was also a source of revenue.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Sita’ in Mauryan period means:
questions.explanation: The maintenance of crown land was done by Sitadhyaksha in the Mauryan period. Revenue collected through this tax was known as 'Sita'.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who of the following was associated with the collection of revenue in Mauryan Mantriparishad ?
questions.explanation: Revenue collection was regulated by Samaharta in Mauryan ministerial council. Antapal looked after border forts while the Pradeshtha was administrator of commissionaries.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Mauryan officers was in charge of weights and measures ?
questions.explanation: Mauryan officer Pautavadhyaksha was in charge of weights and measures while Panyadhyaksha was in charge of the Commerce Department, Sitadhyaksha was the head of the Agriculture Department and Sunadhyaksha was the chief of the slaughterhouse.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Rajjukas were:

options.c: Feudal Lords in the Gupta empire

questions.explanation: ‘Rajjuka’ officials were mentioned in the edicts of Ashoka. Rajjukas were categories of officials in the rural areas, who worked as surveyors combined with judicial functions with assessment duties.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The official 'Agronomai' during Mauryan age was related with which of the following fields?
questions.explanation: During the Mauryan times 'Agronomai' used to collect revenues, monitor irrigation facilities, perform legal administration & looked after road construction. UPPSC has accepted (c) as the answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which among of the following prohibits remarriage?
questions.explanation: It is mentioned in 38th part of Manusmriti that a widower could remarry but a widow had no right to seek remarriage.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The social status assigned to the foreigners in Indian society by Manu was of the –
questions.explanation: The foreign invaders who did not follow priestly customs or traditions (Shakas, Kushans, Hunas, Pratihar) were stated as ‘Fallen Kshatriyas’ in Manusmriti.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II select the correct answer by using the codes given below. List -I List- II A.Chandragupta 1. Piyadashi B.Bindusara 2. Sandrocottus C.Ashoka 3. Amitraghat D.Chanakya 4. Vishnugupta Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: Justin and other Greek authors stated Chandragupta Maurya as “Sandrocottus.” Greek authors mentioned Bindusara as Amitrachates (Amitraghat) while Ashoka was mentioned as Priyadashi in his inscriptions. Vishnugupta is the another name of Chanakya, the prime minister of Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following rulers paid attention to the resource management in Girnar region some centuries before the Christian era? 1. Mahapadma Nanda 2. Chandragupta Maurya 3. Ashoka 4. Rudradaman Select the correct answer using the codes given below : Code :
questions.explanation: Few centuries before the Christian era, the Mauryan emperors, Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka focussed on water resource management in Girnar region. The Governor of Chandragupta Maurya's Western Province Pushyagupt built Sudarshan Lake and the Governor of Emperor Ashok, Tushasp took out canals from the lake. The Junagarh inscription of Shaka ruler Rudradaman describes the works of both Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka. 2nd century A.D., the lake was repaired by the Governor of Rudradaman Suvisakh. According to the question, he did this work after the Christian era. Thus he is not included in the answer, so the correct answer for the question is Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka. * Realizing the need for water, the first ruler who got a lake constructed in the Girnar area, was [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2002]; [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2007] - Chandragupta Maurya * In which inscription are both Chandragupta and Ashoka mentioned? [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004] - Junagarh inscription of Mahakshatrapa Rudradaman

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following inscriptions, Ashoka’s edicts are also found?
questions.explanation: Ashoka’s edicts are also found on Junagarh Inscription of Mahakshtrapa Rudradaman. It also includes the edicts of Gupta ruler Skandagupta. There was an inscription with fourteen edicts of Ashoka on a larger boulder within 2 km of Uparkot fort. The edicts also narrate the story of Sudarshan Lake which was repaired by Rudradaman-I.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is not true about the Barabar hill caves?

options.a: There are in all four caves on the Barabar hill
options.b: Inscriptions of Ashoka are found on the walls of three caves.
options.c: These inscriptions inform us about the dedication of these caves to the Ajivakas
options.d: These inscriptions date back to 6th century BC.

questions.answer_text: These inscriptions date back to 6th century BC.
questions.explanation: Barabar caves are situated in Jahanabad district of Bihar. These caves were hewed out from rocks for monks to live in. There are four caves on the Barabar hill out of which inscriptions of Ashoka are found on the walls of three caves. These caves were used by ascetics from the Ajivaka sect (founded by Makkhali Gosala). These rock-cut caves are related to the Mauryan period (321-184 BC).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched ? 1. Lothal - Ancient Dockyard 2. Sarnath - First Sermon of Buddha 3. Rajgir - Lion Capital of Ashoka 4. Nalanda - Great Seat of Buddhist Learning Select the correct answer using the code given below. Code :
questions.explanation: Lothal-Ancient Dockyard, Sarnath First Sermon of Buddha, Nalanda Great Seat of Buddhist Learning, all these are correct but Rajgir- Lion Capital of Ashoka is not correct. The correct answer would be option (c).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: With reference to the invaders in ancient India, which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
questions.explanation: Correct order is : Greeks-Sakas – Kushans

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below : List-I List-II A. Demetrius 1. Parthian B. Rudradaman 2. Kushana C. Gondophernes 3. Indo- Greek D. Vim 4. Scythean Codes : A B C D
questions.explanation: The correctly matched list is as follows - Demetrius Indo- Greek Rudradaman Scythians Gondophernes Parthian Vim Kushana

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following Indo-Greek rulers issued lead coins ?
questions.explanation: Strato - II issued the lead coins. The tenure of this Indo-Greek ruler is considered from 25 BC to 10 AD.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Both Sankarshana and Vasudeva are depicted on the coins of which of the following rulers?
questions.explanation: Agathocles was a Greco-Bactrian king who ruled around 190 BC - 180 BC. He held Paropamisadae which was a satrapy between Bactria and India. Little is known of him apart from an extensive coinage. He was the first Greco- Bactrian ruler to introduce bilingual legends on his coins, primarily in Greek and Brahmi. He introduced silver coins on which both Sankarshana (Balram) and Vasudev were depicted.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The earliest specimen of ‘Kavya’ style is found in the inscription of :
questions.explanation: The Junagar inscription of Rudradaman (130-150 AD) has been found at Girnar Hills in Gujarat. Rudradaman’s inscription written in Brahmi script was the earliest ever inscription written in perfect Sanskrit language.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who renovated Sudarshan lake without using forced labour ?
questions.explanation: The rock edict of Rudradaman-I at Junagadh (Gujarat) tells about the Sudarshan Lake, which was built originally by the great Mauryan Emperor Chandragupt Maurya's Western Province governor Pushyagupt. It was Rudradaman-I, who renovated Sudarshan Lake without using forced labour.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following metals the Karddamaka Kshatrapas issued and very rare coins?
questions.explanation: Karddamaka ruler's coinage can be categorised into two categories. 1st are those silver coins, which were quite frequent during the kshatrapas rule. 2nd are potin coins. Karddamaka ruler Chastana issued both silver & copper coin. Question is asked about rare coins, so correct answer will be option (a) copper, as copper coins were quite rare during Karddamaka rulers reign.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The largest number of copper coins in northern and northwestern India were issued by ?
questions.explanation: Gold coins were issued by Indo-Greek kings in northern and north-western India while Kushan ruler made it more popular and steady. Kushan rulers had circulated both gold and copper coins vastly in this region.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Kings is credited to have issued gold coins for the first time ?
questions.explanation: Although Indo-Greek rulers made gold coins popular, Vima Kadphises was the first Kushan ruler who issued gold coins. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following introduced gold coins for regular use in India?
questions.explanation: Kushana emperor Vima Kadphises, who was the father of Kanishka-I, had introduced gold coins for regular use in India. He is known as the first king, who introduced gold coins, while Kujul Kadphises circulated copper coins. * Who issued gold coins regularly in ancient India? [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004] - Kushan

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Buddha is depicted on the coins of :
questions.explanation: Buddha is depicted on the coins of Kushana ruler-Kanishka.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which God is found depicted on Yaudheya coins ?
questions.explanation: There are several varieties of Yaudheya copper coins depicting a standing figure of six-headed God Kartikeya along with peacock on the right, found during the reign of the Kushan ruler. The evidences of Yaudheya coins are found from the Puranas, Ashtadhyayi, etc.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched? List-I List-II (Dynasties) (Metals of coin)
questions.explanation: The Satavahana coins are a unique indication. They issued punch-marked coins and produced coins in Lead, Copper, Bronze, Silver and Potin (Copper, Silver & lead mixed) but not in Gold. Thus, option (c) is not correctly matched. Rest of the other types of coins are correctly matched with their dynasties.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was Vikram Samvat started?
questions.explanation: Two other names of Vikram Samvat is Krit and Malav. There is a difference of 470 years between the salvation of Mahavir and Vikram Samvat in Jain holy texts. The salvation date of Mahavir is 527 BC. So, the starting date of Vikram Samvat is 527- 470 = 57 BC.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was Saka Samvat initiated ?
questions.explanation: According to Jain texts, the successor of Vikramaditya (57 B.C.) was defeated by Saka in 135 Vikram Samvat. To celebrate this Victory, Saka started a new calendar called Saka Samvat. Hence it begins from 135-57= 78 AD. Most of the historians believe that the Kushan ruler Kanishka was its originator.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: A Chalukya inscription is dated in the year 556 of the Saka era. It is equivalent to–
questions.explanation: Saka era was launched by Kanishka in 78 AD. If Chalukya inscription is dated in the year 556, then it is equivalent to 556 + 78 = 634 A.D.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following will be the year of Saka Samvat in December, 2009.
questions.explanation: Saka Samvat has been adopted as the national calendar in India. It started in 78 AD. So, in December 2009 according to Saka Samvat 2009-78 = 1931 will be the year of Saka Samvat.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: How much is the year difference between the Saka Samvat and Vikram Samvat?
questions.explanation: Currently, for date and year, Gregorian Calendar is being used which is internationally used civil calendar. In order to get Vikram Samvat (57 B.C.), 57 is to be added in the current calendar and to get the Saka Samvat (78 AD), 78 is to be subtracted from current calendar. Hence, Vikram Samvat is 2025+57 = 2082 and Saka Samvat is 2019 – 78 = 1941. Hence, the difference between Vikram Samvat and Saka Samvat is 2082 – 1947 = 135 years. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the date of Sarnath Buddhist image inscription of Kanishka ?
questions.explanation: The date of Buddha inscription of Sarnath which belongs to Kanishka is dated 81 AD. This inscription was established after three years of Kanishka’s coronation. * In which year, the coronation of Kushan king Kanishka was held? [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1991] - 78 A.D.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following name of contemporaries of Kanishka and select the correct answer from codes given below : (i) Ashvaghosha (ii) Vasumitra (iii)Kalidas (iv) Kamban Code :
questions.explanation: Ashvaghosha was the poet laureate of Kanishka, whose major compositions were Saundaranand, Buddhacharita and Sariputraprakaran. Vasumitra was also a dependent poet of Kanishka, who headed the IVth Buddhist Council. While Kalidas was related to the Gupta period and Kamban was not the contemporary of Kanishka. So, option (c) is the correct answer. * Ashvaghosha was contemporary of [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2008] - Kanishka

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is not associated with the Court of Kanishka ?
questions.explanation: Parsva, Vasumitra, Ashvaghosa, Nagarjuna, Charaka and Mathara were the scholars in the Court of Kanishka. Charaka is known as the Court physician of Kanishka. However, Maharshi Patanjali belonged to Shunga period and was the author of Mahabhasya.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who of the following did not adorn the court of Kanishka- I ?
questions.explanation: See the explanation of above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following cities is not mentioned in the Rabatak inscription of Kanishka?
questions.explanation: Rabatak inscriptions were found in the year 1993 from Rabatak near Surkh Kotal, Afghanistan. They were written in Greek script and Bactrian language and belonged to the ruler of Kushana dynasty, Kanishka. There are four names of cities inscribed on it namely - Saket, Kaushambi, Pataliputra and Sri Champa. The name of Shravasti was not inscribed on it.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Read these statements– Assertion (A) : Kushans traded through Gulf of Persian and Red sea. Reason (R) : Their well organised naval force base was highly qualified. In context to the above which is the correct answer : Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: A lot of evidence regarding ports and trading centres has been found from the excavations of Periplus of the Erythraean Sea and Arikamedu which proves that Kushanas trade was operated through Persian Bay and the Red Sea. But none of the evidence described the naval forces of Kushanas.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Ayurvedacharyas was educated at Taxila University ?
questions.explanation: Taxila University was the junction where students of different countries met each other and exchanged their knowledge. Kautilya, Chandragupta Maurya and Ayurvedacharya Charak, King Prasenjit of Kosala, Ayurvedacharya Jivak of Bimbisar, Vasubandhu, etc. studied at Taxila University. Thus, options (c) and (d), both are correct.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Between which of the following was the ancient town of Takshashila located?
questions.explanation: Takshashila was established during 6th or 7th century BC. It was a town and an important archaeological site in Rawalpindi district of Punjab, Pakistan. It is situated between the rivers Jhelum and Indus.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Gandhar Art 1. Menander B. Junagarh Rock 2. Patika inscription C. Milindapanho 3. Kushanas D. Taxila 4. Rudradaman I inscription Codes : A B C D
questions.explanation: The correctly matched list is as follows– List-I List-II Gandhar Art – Kushanas Junagarh Rock – Rudradaman I inscription Milindapanho – Menander Taxila inscription – Patika

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Gandhara School of art is the synthesis of:
questions.explanation: Gandhara is noted for the distinctive Gandhara style of Buddhist art, which was developed from the merger of Greek, Syrian, Persian and Indian artistic influences. It flourished during the Saka and Kushan era. It is also known as Greco-Buddhist, Indo-Greek or Greco-Roman, as the subject of the art was only Buddha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Bamiyan of Afghanistan was famous for –
questions.explanation: Bamiyan of Afghanistan was famous for Buddha’s statues which were constructed by cutting the hills of Bamiyan, but Taliban (in 2001) destroyed all the statues.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following inscription gives the information about two Ashwamedha Yajnas performed by the king Pushyamitra Shung?
questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Shunga was the commander of last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha. He founded the Shunga dynasty killing Brihadratha in 184 BCE. Ayodhya inscription gives us the information that two Ashwamedha Yagnas were performed by the King Pushyamitra Shunga.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The writer of Mahabhashya ‘Patanjali’ was contemporary of–
questions.explanation: Patanjali (the author of Mahabhashya) was contemporary to Pushyamitra Shunga (184-148 BC).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which dynasty was most powerful after Maurya in Southern India -
questions.explanation: Satavahana dynasty was the most powerful after Mauryans in the South. According to Puranas, Sindhuk, Simuka or Shiprak established the Satavahana dynasty after the assassination of Kanva king Susharma. * Simuka was the founder of which of the following dynasties? [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2008] - Satavahana

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which among the following was the earliest dynasty ?
questions.explanation: Satavahana is the most ancient dynasty among the above mentioned options. It was founded and ruled by Simuk in near about second century BC.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The capital of the Satavahanas was located at –
questions.explanation: The actual capital of Satavahanas was located at Paithan or Pratisthan, although their initial capital is believed to be Amravati. According to the Puranas, the founder of Satavahana dynasty is believed to be King Simuka. * Which place was the capital of Satvahanas? [U.P. Lower (Spl) (Pre) 2008] - Pratisthan

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: For which of the following rulers “Ekabrahmana” has been used?
questions.explanation: In the Nashik inscription of Gautami Balashri, her son Gautamiputra Shatakarni is called “Ekabrahmana” which is interpreted by some as “unrivalled Brahmana” thus indicating a Brahmin origin.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : In Satavahana period, Sanskrit along with Prakrit and other folk languages were developed. Reason (R) : Satavahana Kings promoted the use of Sanskrit and other folk languages for literary writings. Choose the correct answer using the codes given.

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: In the Satavahana period, Sanskrit along with Prakrit and other folk languages were developed. Satavahana king promoted the use of Sanskrit and other folk languages for literary writings.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: With reference to the Satavahana Rulers which of the following statement/s is/are true? 1. The Satavahana Kings were the nurturers of Prakrit language. 2. Public aspect of the arts got more encouragement during the Satavahana period. Select the correct answer using the codes given below. Codes
questions.explanation: Satavahana rulers patronised Prakrit more than Sanskrit. Political inscriptions also threw some light on the rare use of Sanskrit Literature. Also public aspect of the arts got more encouragement during Satavahana period. Examples of architecture and sculptures found from the Satvahana era are associated with Buddhism.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The rulers of which of the following dynasty have been called as 'Shriparvatiya' in Puranas?
questions.explanation: Rulers of the Ikshvaku dynasty are called 'Shriparvatiya' in Puranas. They were Lords under the Patronage of Satvahanas, but after their decline, Ikshvakus declared their independence. Shrisantmula was the founder of this dynasty.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Kings was a Patron of Jainism ?
questions.explanation: Kharavela of Chedi dynasty was the king of Kalinga present-day in Odisha, India. Much of the available information about Kharavela comes from the undated and partially damaged Hathigumpha inscription, plus a few other minor inscriptions found in Udayagiri Caves, in present-day Odisha. This is the only known source of Kharavela inscriptions. The Kharavela is believed to be a follower of Jainism. * The King of Kalinga Kharavela was related to which dynasty? [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2015]; [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2008] - Chedi * The inscription of Hathigumpha is the source of information about which king? [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2018] - Kharavela

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History

questions.subject: History

questions.explanation: King of Vakataka, Pravarsena-I had performed four Ashwamedhas. He also performed many Vedic oblations. Pravarsena-II, another ruler of the same dynasty, was interested in literature, who wrote ‘Setubandha.’

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who is known as the Napoleon of India?
questions.explanation: Historian V.A. Smith in his composition ‘Early History of India’ called Samudragupta (335-375 AD) of Gupta dynasty as ‘Napoleon of India’ for his great military conquests.

questions.explanation: Copperplate inscription of Samudragupta from Nalanda and Gaya describes param Bhagavata title of Samudragupta. Although UPPSC has given option (c) as correct answer UGC has accepted Samudragupta as right answer.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: An inscription by which of the following is found on the pillar containing Prayag Prasasti of Samudragupta?
questions.explanation: Prayag Prashasti is the name given to Allahabad pillar. It is an Ashokan Pillar but has 4 different inscriptions: Ashokan inscription in Brahmi script. Queen edict regarding the charitable deed of Ashoka’s wife, Karuvaki. Samudragupta inscription written by Harisena in Sanskrit language and Brahmi script and Jahangir inscription in Persian.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Prithivyah Pratham Veer’ was the title of –
questions.explanation: In his book ‘A Political History of the Imperial Guptas’, Tej Ram Sharma describes Ashvamedha Yajna which was done by Samudragupta. After this ritual, he assumed the title of ‘Prithivyama Pratiratha’ which means that a man who has no rival on the earth ( The first brave man on the Earth). Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission excluded this question from the evaluation.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Gupta Kings had another name Devagupta ?
questions.explanation: Another name of Gupta ruler Chandragupta-II ‘Vikramaditya’ is found as Devagupta. Its evidence has been obtained from Sanchi and Vakataka inscriptions. Apart from the above-mentioned names, he is also known as Devaraja and Devashri.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The iron column, located in the courtyard of Delhi’s Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque is retention of –
questions.explanation: Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription’ acquired from Mehrauli in Delhi is located in the centre of the courtyard of Quwwat-ul-Islam msoque. It describes a king named “Chandra” which is assumed as Chandragupta II of Gupta clan. According to recognition, the Mehrauli iron pillar was situated at Vishnugiri near Udaigiri Hills during the period of Chandragupta II around 410 AD. Chandragupta II was the devotee of Lord Vishnu. He constructed this iron pillar in respect of Lord Vishnu. Emblem bearer of Lord Vishnu ‘Garuda” was engraved on the apex of the pillar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who is known as ‘Saka-conqueror’?
questions.explanation: Gupta ruler Chandragupta- II ‘Vikramaditya’ was known as the ‘Saka Conqueror’ as he eliminated Saka power by defeating last Saka king Rudrasimha- III in the first decade of the 5th century. He adopted the title of 'Sakari' after this victory. He issued silver coins (Rupak) on this occasion.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: With reference to Chandragupta – II, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The strongest evidence in the context of Shaka Victory is the silver coins of this King. 2. The weight of these coins used to be about 33 grains. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :
questions.explanation: After victory over Shaka, Chandragupta II released silver coins. These coins usually weigh around 30 to 33 grain. Hence both statement are true.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which dynasty was distracted the most by the Hunas invasion?
questions.explanation: The first invasion of Hunas took place during the reign of Skanda-gupta and Hunas were comprehensively defeated by him. This invasion was just like a raid, and there was not lasting impact on India, but this invasion intensified the decline of the Gupta Empire. Hunas annexed many regions of the northwest in the transition period of 5th-6th centuries after the death of Skandagupta. * The Hunas invaded India during the reign of [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2006] - Skandagupta * Which Gupta Ruler conquered Hunas? [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2004] - Skandagupta * Which Gupta ruler defeated Hunas? [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2015] - Skandagupta

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: From which inscription is it known that Skandagupta defeated Hunas?
questions.explanation: Bhitari Pillar inscription is found at the place known as Bhitari in Saidpur tehsil of district Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh. The description of the war between Skandagupta and Hunas is mentioned in Bhitari Pillar inscription. It is noteworthy that the first Indian invasion of Hunas took place during the reign of Skandagupta in which Hunas were badly defeated by Skandagupta.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Mandsaur – Prashasti presents the details of the achievements of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Vatsabhatta or Vatsabhatti was a contemporary of Kumar-gupta-I, composed the Mandsaur-Prashasti at Malwa. The Mandsaur-Prashasti presents the details of achievements of Kumargupta-I. It also describes that the silk workers had constructed a sun temple here which was repaired by Bandhuvarma.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies

questions.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Kumargupta I : Mandsaur inscription Patik : Takshashila inscription Chandragupta II : Udayagiri cave inscription Samudragupta : Eran inscription No records of Prabhavati Gupta has been obtained from Udayagiri Cave inscription.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements with reference to early trade: 1. There are references of numerous river-ports in ancient India. 2. There were large entrepots of goods and traffic. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: In ancient India, rivers and ports were major centers of trade and transport. During the Indus Valley Civilization, ports like Lothal, as well as warehouses at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, provide evidence of large trading hubs. In historical times, rivers like the Ganga and Kaveri served as important routes for trade and transportation. Ports such as Muziris and Sopara were famous for trade with Rome and Southeast Asia. In ancient India, large warehouses were used for the storage of goods, which facilitated trade. Thus, both statements 1 and 2 are true.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following ports handled the North Indian trade during the Gupta period ?
questions.explanation: The Tamralipti port in Bengal was a prominent port during the Gupta period from where trade was conducted with southeast Asia, China, Lanka, Java, Sumatra as well as northern India. Western coast had an important port of Bhrigu Kachchha (Bharuch) from where Gupta rulers used to trade with western countries.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following is known for his Ayurvedic thematic composition during Gupta period?
questions.explanation: Sushruta is called the father of surgery. He was a resident of Kashi. It is believed that his period was around 600 BC. Shaunak was the sage of the Rigveda. Shudraka was a dramatist of the Gupta period (literateur). Saumill is a playwright of Gupta period who has been remembered by Kalidasa with language and poetry. Thus, none of the above had worked in the field of medicine during the Gupta period. Since the Gupta period begins with 275-AD (Sri Gupta), which is about 875 years later than the valid period of Sushruta (usually 600 BC), it is not reasonable to consider Sushruta a contemporary of the Gupta period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who of the following among the Nine Gems of Chandragupta was associated with Astrology ?
questions.explanation: The Nine Gems of Chandragupta II were (1) Kalidasa (Poet), (2) Dhanvantari (Physician), (3) Varahamihira (Astronomer), (4) Amar Singh (Lexicographer), (5) Shanku (Architect) (6) Kshapanak (Astrologer), (7) Vararuchi (Grammarian), (8) Vetal Bhatta (Magician) (9) Ghata Karpara (Diplomat).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Gupta gold coin was called -
questions.explanation: Gold coins issued by Gupta rulers were known as Dinar. According to Fa hien, people used Dinar for daily business.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The silver coins issued by the Guptas were called :
questions.explanation: The silver coins issued by the Gupta ruler were known as “Rupaka”. The Gupta coins have been found from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Orissa. Bharatpur (Bayana) in Rajasthan is the place from where a maximum number of coins have been found.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who of the following was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins ?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta-I was the first Gupta ruler who issued the coins. There is no evidence available for issuance of coins by Ghatokacha and Srigupta, the early rulers of Gupta dynasty. Samudragupta also issued various types of coins, but his tenure was after Chandragupta-I.

questions.question: Who was the first Gupta ruler to issue silver coins?
questions.explanation: See the explanation of above question.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The first inscriptional evidence of the Satipratha has been found from –
questions.explanation: The first evidence of ‘Satipratha’ has been found from the inscription of Eran. This inscription belongs to 510 AD in which practice of Sati has been mentioned for a lady who was the wife of war commander named ‘Gopraj.’

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In Ancient India, which dynasty’s rule is considered as the Golden Age?
questions.explanation: Gupta period in ancient India is considered as the golden age due to the excellent development in the field of art and culture.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of administrative division during the Gupta Period?
questions.explanation: During Gupta period, the empire was divided into provinces named Bhukti. Empire Bhukti Vishayas Vithi Gram (King) (Uparik) (Vishayapati) (Aayulan and Vithimahattar) (Gramik/Ashtakuladhikari) (Provincial administration of Gupta Period)

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: During which age, did women enjoy equality with men ?
questions.explanation: Except for the Vedic age, the situation of women was never good in ancient India. In the age of Gupta, Maurya and Chola, the evidence of inferior condition of women has been found. Thus condition of women with men cannot be compared in any age.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the valid tax according to Hindu law?
questions.explanation: In every religious text, the land revenue rate is 1/6th of the produce.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In ancient India, the irrigation tax was called –
questions.explanation: In ancient India, the irrigation tax was known as ‘Udakbhog.’ Hiranya was the cash tax in the Mauryan period. The land tax was called Udrang in Gupta inscriptions. ‘Uparnika’ was the tax on farmers living on the land.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A) : The main feature of the agrarian structure in the post-Gupta period was the development of feudalism. options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Option (a) is correct because both assertion (A) and reason (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 3rd AD, Warangal was famous for–
questions.explanation: Warangal was famous for production of iron equipment. ‘Agaria’ people lived there, and iron making was the traditional occupation for them.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The term ‘Kausheya’ has been used for –
questions.explanation: In Gupta and later Gupta period, the word ‘Kausheya’ was used to denote silk.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who amongst the following had defeated Huna ruler Mihirakula?
questions.explanation: Mihirkula was of Central Asian Huna origin who was one of the most important Hephthalite emperors. The Gwalior inscription showed his territory which included Gwalior. Mihirkula suffered a defeat by the Aulikara king Yasodharman of Malwa in 528 A.D. (Other Sources mention 495 A.D.).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The game of ‘Chess’ is said to have originated in –
questions.explanation: The game of chess originated in India during the Gupta period was known as ‘Chaturanga.’ It reached Iran and then Europe from India.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The system of philosophy propounded by Kapila Muni is :
questions.explanation: Sankhya Darshan is one of the most ancient philosophical schools of India. Maharshi Kapila is known as the ‘Acharya’ of Sankhya Darshan. He composed ‘Sankhya Sutra’ and Tatvasamas. * ‘Sankhya’ Philosophy is propounded by [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2010] - Kapila

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who propagated ‘Yoga Darshan’?
questions.explanation: Maharshi Patanjali is known as the founder of ‘Yoga Darshan.’ Although the history of yoga in Indian tradition is very old. The description about yoga is found in Upanishad, Mahabharat, Bhagavad Geeta, Jain and Buddha texts. However, Maharshi Patanjali explained it as a compact philosophical theory. So it is called as 'Patanjali Darshan’.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The founder of school of Navya-Nyaya was:
questions.explanation: The foundation of Navya-Nyaya school was the result of the revolutionary work of Mithila based scholar Udayana or Udayanacharya and after that Gangesh.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Nyaya Philosophical system was propagated by:
questions.explanation: ‘Nyaya Darshan’ was propagated by Gautama who is also known as ‘Akshapada.’ The word ‘Nyaya’ means decision or logic. Nyaya Darshan recognizes the existence of 16 substances or elements. The original text of Nyaya Darshan is 'Nyayasutra' which is the masterpiece of Gautama. Maharshi Kapila propagated “Sankhya Darshan’ while Jaimini propagated ‘Purva Mimansa.’
