questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Photosynthesis using the invisible part of the sunlight is done by some –
questions.explanation: The bacteria which are found in the deep sea, for example green sulphur bacteria, uses infrared radiations for photosynthesis to produce energy.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following energy conversions takes place in carrying out the process of photosynthesis ?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process used by plants to convert light energy into chemical energy. Photosynthesis can be represented by using following chemical equation-Where CO2 = Carbon dioxide H2 O = Water C6 H12O6 = Glucose O2 = Oxygen

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Diffusion of light in the atmosphere takes place due to :
questions.explanation: Sunlight is the mixture of different colours. When it passes through the atmosphere it is scattered by the air molecules, particles of dust and other subtle materials which are present in the pathway.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The colour of light is determined by its
questions.explanation: The colour of light is determined by its wavelength. Different colours have different wavelengths. In the visible spectrum of light, the wavelength of red colour is largest and violet colour has the shortest wavelength.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following colours of white light is least deviated by the glass prism?
questions.explanation: Speeds of different colours of white light are same in a vacuum but differs in different matters. Thus, the refractive index of any matter differs for different colours of light. The speed of violet light is minimum and the speed of red light is maximum in the glass. So the refractive index of glass is maximum for violet light and minimum for the red light and the violet light is most deviated and red light is least deviated by the glass prism.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Red light is used in traffic signals because :

options.c: It is visible to people even with bad eyesight.

questions.explanation: The wavelength of red colour is highest while of violet colour is lowest. Dispersal is inverse to wavelength so red light can be seen from far away more clear. That's why the red colour is used in traffic signals.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Assertion (A): The danger signal is made up of red colour. Reason (R) : Red colour is scattered the least. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The primary reason why the red colour is used for danger signals is that red light has the highest wavelength and scattered least by air molecules so that it can be seen from far away. The appearance of the red colour of Sun at the sunset is due to the fact that neighbouring colours are scattered away in the path and light reaching the observer is predominantly red. That is why the Sun appears red to us. * Red light signal is used as a danger signal because [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2008; U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011; U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2005; U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1995] - Red light is scattered least * Sky is blue because [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 1998] - Short waves are scattered more than long waves by atmosphere * Blue colour of the sky is due to [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) (Re. Exam) 2015] - Scattering of light

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The red colour of the Sun at sunset and sunrise is due to –
questions.explanation: The intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to its wavelength and the wavelength of violet and blue is low, thus they scatter more. This is the main cause for the blue colour of the sky. As we know that sunlight consists of seven colours, of these, red has the maximum wavelength. During sunrise and sunset, the rays have to travel a larger part of the atmosphere because they are very close to the horizon. Therefore light other than red is mostly scattered away. Most of the red light which is least scattered enters our eyes. Hence, the Sun appears red. The rainbow is caused by reflection, refraction and dispersion of light in water droplets resulting in a spectrum of light appearing in the sky. Thus, statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: An astronaut sees the colour of the sky as –
questions.explanation: The colour of the sky for an astronaut is black. It is because of the fact that in the space there is no atmosphere. In space, there are no air particles against which the sunlight can strike, get reflected or scattered. Hence, astronauts see everything as black. * When we see the sky from a plane at high altitude, then it seems [U.P.P.S.C. (R.I.) 2014] - Black

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The number of colours contained in the sunlight is –
questions.explanation: As we all know the sunlight is a white light and it consists of seven colours. The splitting of light into its different components (VIBGYOR) i.e. violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red is called the dispersion of light. A prism is used to disperse light into its different components.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The (Green) Grass appears green to us because :

options.a: It reflects green colour light to our eyes
options.c: It reflects all other colour lights except that of green colour

questions.answer_text: It reflects green colour light to our eyes
questions.explanation: The colour we see on the surface of an object is not actually the colour in that surface. If a surface looks green, it means that it absorbs all colours of the spectrum except green. It looks black to our eyes in case no colour is reflected. If an object is white it reflects all light.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The concept of expanding universe is based on –
questions.explanation: The concept of expanding universe is based on Doppler effect. It was named after Christian Doppler, who first came up with the idea in 1842. Edwin Hubble used the Doppler Effect to determine that universe is expanding. Hubble found that the light from distant galaxies was shifted towards lower frequencies, to the red end of the spectrum. This is known as a red Doppler shift or a red-shift.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In driving a car which type of mirror would you like to use for observing traffic behind you?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives a much wider field of view of the traffic behind you than a plain mirror of the same size. It always forms an erect and diminished image and they also have a wider field of view as they are curved outwards.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The image formed by astronomical telescope is
questions.explanation: Astronomical telescope consists of two convex lenses: Objective and Eyepiece. The final image formed by the astronomical telescope is inverted, virtual and highly magnified.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Assertion (A):Black hole is such a celestial existence which cannot be seen by telescope. Reason (R) :The gravitational field of black hole is much strong that even light does not escape from it. Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: A black hole is an object which is so compact that its gravitational force is strong enough to prevent light or anything else from escaping. By this reason, one can't see it with the telescope.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The number of images of an object placed between two parallel mirrors is :
questions.explanation: When an object is placed in between two parallel plane mirrors, then the number of images formed will be infinite. Each image will be the result of an image. When two plane mirrors are inclined at an angle of q, then the number of images formed by the object between them is (If the value of 360° q is even), or  360°      θ (If the value of 360° q is odd).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following colours is seen in the middle of a Rainbow ?
questions.explanation: The correct order of colors of the rainbow is Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo and Violet. Thus it is clear that 'Green' Color is seen in the middle of a rainbow (VIBGYOR). * The terminal colour bands of the rainbow are [U.P. Lower Sub. (Mains) 2015] - Violet and Red

questions.exam_tag: U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2013; U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Spl.) ; (Pre) 2010; U.P.P.C.S. (Spl.) (Pre) 2008 ; U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2002
questions.question: An air bubble in water will act like a :
questions.explanation: An air bubble in water, whose surface is convex will act like a concave lens (divergent lens). The refractive index of water is more than that of air. Thus the nature of lens of submerged water bubble is changed.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The minimum height of a plane mirror to see the full size image of a person is equal to –

options.b: Half the height of the person
options.c: One-fourth the height of the person
options.d: Double the height of the person

questions.answer_text: Half the height of the person
questions.explanation: The minimum height of a plane mirror to enable a person to see full image is 1/2 of his height. According to the principle of reflection, the angle of incidence is equal to angle of reflection. When the ray of light travels from bottom to top of a person and reaches his eyes then he is able to see the clear image. The ray from the foot strikes the mirror at its bottom and reaches his eye after reflecting from the mirror. Thus, the height of the mirror must equal to half the height of the person.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The minimum height of mirror required to see whole stand up image of a man of height 1.50 metre shall be
questions.explanation: In order to see full-length image, the minimum height of the mirror required is half of a person’s height. Therefore, minimum height of mirror required = 1.50/2 metre = 0.75 metre.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The radius of curvature of the plane mirror is :
questions.explanation: A plane mirror is a spherical mirror with an infinite radius of curvature. As we know that the reflection in the plane mirror forms at the same distance at which the object is placed in front of the mirror. That is, do = distance of the object from the mirror di = distance of reflection from the mirror (here r = radius of curvature) But for the plane mirror do = –di Thus, the radius of curvature of plane mirror is considered as infinity.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The least distance of distinct vision is (cm.) :
questions.explanation: The normal human eye can focus a sharp image of an object on the eye if the object located anywhere from infinity to a certain point called the "Near point". The minimum distance of an object from eye to have its clear image is called "least distance of distinct vision". It is about 25 cm for the normal eye and denoted by 'D'.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following statement is not true for a person suffering from hypermetropia?

options.a: The person can see far objects distinctly.
options.b: The focal length of the lens is large.
options.c: The image of the close objects is focused behind the retina.
options.d: A concave lens is used to correct this defect.

questions.answer_text: A concave lens is used to correct this defect.
questions.explanation: Far-sightedness (hypermetropia) is a common vision problem, affecting about a fourth of the population. People with hypermetropia can see distant objects very well but have difficulty in focusing on objects that are close. This vision problem occurs when light rays entering the eye focused behind the retina rather than directly on it. The eyeball of a farsighted person is shorter than normal. A convex lens is used to correct this defect.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following lenes is used to minimize Myopia?
questions.explanation: A concave lens is used to minimize the defect of myopia.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A myopic eye can be corrected by using a :
questions.explanation: Myopia or near-sightedness is a refractive error which means that the eye does not bend or refract light properly to a single focus to see the image clearly. In Myopia, close objects look clear but distant objects appear blurred. It is corrected by using a concave lens.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The focusing in the eye is done by :

options.a: Change in the convexity of the lens
options.b: To and fro movement of the lens
options.c: To and fro movement of the retina
options.d: Change in the refractive index of the eye fluid

questions.answer_text: Change in the convexity of the lens
questions.explanation: We see the world around us because of the way our eyes bend (refract) light. The refractive or bending power of the cornea and humor is constant. However, that of the lens can be changed by changing its shape. That is by making it more or less convex so that light can be properly focused on the retina. The greater the lens convexity or bulge the more it bends the light. The flatter the lens, the less it bends that light.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science

options.a: Mirage is an optical illusion arising due to total internal reflection of light
options.b: Concave mirrors are used in searchlights

options.d: Convex mirror with a small aperture is used by doctors to examine, ear, nose or throat of a patient.

questions.answer_text: Convex mirror with a small aperture is used by doctors to examine, ear, nose or throat of a patient.
questions.explanation: Head Mirror is mostly used by doctors for the examination of ear, nose, and throat. It comprises a circular concave mirror, with a small hole in the middle and is attached to a head-band. Hence statement (d) is not correct. Remaining statements are correct.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The mirror, which is used in searchlights, is –
questions.explanation: Concave mirror is used in the headlights of cars and in searchlights. A light placed at the focus of a concave lens can form a parallel beam and is used in car headlights and searchlights.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A dentist mirror is a –
questions.explanation: Concave mirrors are used by dentists because at a short range (object distances less than the focal length) they produce magnified, upright images. It is useful to have a magnified image of a tooth when you’re looking for or repairing cavities, cracks or other abnormalities.

questions.question: Power of the sunglass is –
questions.explanation: The power of the sunglass is 0 dioptre.

questions.question: Two glass lenses of same focal length, one being convex and the other concave, are kept in contact, the combination will act as :
questions.explanation: If two glass lenses of same focal length, one being convex and the other concave are kept in contact then resultant focal length of the combination will be infinity and it will act as a plane glass sheet.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The image formed on Retina is :
questions.explanation: The image formed on Retina is real, inverted and smaller than the object. The signals for image formation are sent via the optic nerve to the brain, which ultimately processes the image and allows us to see. However, the image formed on Retina is inverted but on the basis of our experience, we see a straight image.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Retina of the eye is comparable to which of the following parts of a traditional camera?
questions.explanation: The back of your eye is lined with a layer known as the retina. The retina operates in a similar way to the film inside a traditional (non-digital) camera. The middle part of the retina (known as the macula) takes care of your sharp vision. Your retina's nerve cells change light rays into electrical impulses and then send them to the brain through the optic nerve.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In long-sightedness, images are formed at following :
questions.explanation: In long-sightedness (Hypermetropia) the image of a nearby object is formed behind the retina. It results in close objects appearing blurry. The condition occurs in case the eyeball is too short or the focal length of the eye lens has been increased. The long-sightedness is corrected by the convex lens.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science

questions.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Relative humidity decreases with increasing air temperature. Reason (R): Absolute humidity increases with increasing evaporation. Select the correct answer from the codes given below:

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
options.c: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Relative humidity decreases with increasing air temperature. This is true. Relative humidity is the percentage of moisture the air holds relative to the maximum it can hold at that temperature. Warmer air can hold more moisture, so even if the absolute amount of water in the air stays the same, the relative humidity decreases as the temperature rises. • Absolute humidity increases with increasing evaporation. This is also true. Absolute humidity is the actual amount of water vapor in the air. Evaporation increases the amount of water vapor in the air, thus increasing absolute humidity. However, (R) doesn’t explain (A). The reason relative humidity decreases with increasing temperature is due to the increased moisture-holding capacity of warmer air, not simply because absolute humidity might increase.

The earthen pitcher is made of mud and has many minute pores. It is through these pores that the water, placed inside the pitcher, oozes out. Now to evaporate, the water needs to absorb heat, which will change it to vapour. questions.answer_text: Water starts boiling at a higher temperature due to high pressure
questions.explanation: Food can be cooked faster in a pressure cooker since the boiling point of water increases with increase in pressure. As the water boils, the steam produced cannot evaporate so the pressure inside the cooker increases. The boiling point of water now becomes about 120o C. The load pin fixed on the heavy aluminum lid prevents any escape of steam. The rubber ring around the lid deals the liquid inside. Thus food gets cooked faster in a pressure cooker. Pressure cookers are more common in the mountains where elevation is high. At higher elevations, atmospheric pressure is lower and therefore water boils at lower temperature. In order to make up for that difference, people use pressure cookers. * Why does food cook faster in a pressure cooker? [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2002] - The increased pressure increases the boiling point.

options.c: Weight kept on hole at top and food being cooked

questions.answer_text: Area of hole on the top and weight kept on it
questions.explanation: In a pressure cooker the food is cooked with the boiling of water. Boiling point is increased inside a pressure cooker by increasing the pressure. This pressure can be adjusted by changing the weight placed on the top of the cooker lid. The pressure (and cooking temperature) also depends upon area of the hole in the lid. The principle of pressure cooking is to maintain a temperature of about 120°C inside the cooker as opposed to a temperature of 100°C attained in open vessels. The weight is designed in such a way that it will kick when the pressure inside just exceeds about one atmospheric gauge thereby releasing the excess pressure. This is the pressure at which the boiling point is about 120°C. Once the requisite pressure and temperature is attained, more heat input (by increasing the temperature of the flame) results in more steam generated which is released through the lid and hence the cooking temperature remains the same, which is about 120°C. Thus, temperature at which the food is cooked does not depend upon temperature of the flame.

When it reaches the Earth, some is reflected back to space (about 35%), some is absorbed by the atmosphere (about 14%), and some is absorbed in the Earth's surface (about 51%). The insolation received by the Earth is in shortwave form and heats up its surface. The Earth after being heated itself becomes a radiating body and it radiates energy to the atmosphere in longwave form. This energy heats up the atmosphere from below. This process is known as terrestrial radiation. The longwave terrestrial radiation is absorbed by the atmospheric gases particularly by carbon dioxide and the other greenhouse gases. questions.question: How two identical bulbs should be connected to get maximum light? 1. Both are connected in series. 2. Both are connected in parallel. Select the correct answer using the code given below : Code :
questions.explanation: Bulbs in parallel are brighter than bulbs in series. In a parallel circuit the voltage for each bulb is the same as the voltage in the circuit while the parallel combination of resistors reduces the effective resistance of the circuit. The power dissipated by a bulb is given by P = V2 /R, where V is the voltage of the light bulb and R is the elec-trical resistance. The total resistance of the series circuit is Rseries = R + R = 2R. The total resistance of the parallel circuit is 1/Rparallel = 1/R + 1/R or Rparallel = R/2. Thereby, the power for the light bulbs in series is Pseries = V2 /2R and the power for the light bulbs in parallel is Pparallel = 2V2 /R Hence, from the above equations it is clear that in parallel circuit the bulbs will shine brightly.

So, Resistance value of resistor = (A × 10 + B) × 10C = (1 × 10 + 5) × 100 = 15 × 1 = 15 Ohm (Ω) Current (i) = Voltage (V) Resistance (R) = 15 15 = 1 ampere Hence, the current flowing through the resistor is 1 ampere.

questions.explanation: When superconductivity was discovered in 1911, it was found only at temperatures close to absolute zero (– 273.15°C). But since then, researchers have steadily uncovered materials that superconduct at higher temperatures. In recent years, scientists have accelerated that progress by focusing on hydrogen-rich materials at high pressure. In 2019 it was discovered that lanthanum hydride (LaH10) becomes a superconductor at around 250-260 K under a pressure of 170 gigapascals. In 2020, a near room-temperature superconductor (around 15°C or 288 K) made from hydrogen, carbon and sulphur under pressures of around 270 gigapascals was described in a paper in research magazine Nature . This is currently the highest temperature at which any material has shown superconductivity.

questions.question: The resistance of a semiconductor on heating :
questions.explanation: With the increase in temperature, the conductivity of the semiconductor material increases. As with increase in temperature, outermost electrons acquire energy and hence by acquiring energy, the outermost electrons leave the shell of the atom. Hence, with an increase in temperature, number of carriers in the semiconductor material increases which leads to increase in the conductivity of the material. So we can say that the semiconductor material has negative temperature coefficient i.e. with an increase in temperature, resistance decreases.

questions.question: Kalpakkam is famous–
questions.explanation: Kalpakkam (Chennai, Tamil Nadu) is known for its nuclear plants and affiliated research installations. These include the Madras Atomic Power Station (MAPS), a nuclear power plant, and the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR- established in 1971), an affiliate of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) and the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC). Madras Atomic Power Station (MAPS) is a comprehensive nuclear power production, fuel reprocessing, and waste treatment facility that includes plutonium fuel fabrication for fast breeder reactors (FBRs). It is also India's first fully indigenously constructed nuclear power station, with two units each generating 220 MWe of electricity (operated by NPCIL). Kalpakkam is also home to India's first large scale fast breeder reactor of 500 MWe (under construction) called the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor operated by BHAVINI and will also be the site of first two FBR-600 commercial fast breeder reactors. A beachhead at Kalpakkam also hosts India's first indigenous pressurised (light) water reactor (PWR). The 80 MW reactor was developed by Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) as the land-based prototype of the nuclear power unit for India's nuclear submarines. * The Indira Gandhi Atomic Research Centre is located in [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2004] - Tamil Nadu

questions.question: What is true for Kalpakkam Fast Breeder Reactor? 1. In it, natural uranium will be used as a fuel. 2. In it, Plutonium carbide and natural uranium carbide mixture will be used as a fuel. 3. More than 200 MW atomic electricity will be produced from it. Choose the correct answer from the following alternatives.
questions.explanation: Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR-being operated since 1985) at the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR), Kalpakkam has a capacity of 13 MWe and uses plutonioum-uranium carbide as a fuel and liquid sodium as coolant. The FBTR is a forerunner to the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR), which is underconstruction at Kalpakkam. The indigenously designed industrial scale prototype FBR of 500 MWe capacity is in an advanced stage of commissioning at Kalpakkam. Indigenously produced Mixed Uranium & Plutonium Oxide will be used as the fuel in the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam. Fast breeder reactors, or FBRs, in general produce more fissile material than they consume. The PFBR in Kalpakkam will use a mixed oxide of plutonium-239 – derived from reprocessed spent fuel from the thermal pressurised heavy water reactors – and uranium-238 as fuel to generate energy in a nuclear reaction. This reaction will also produce – or 'breed' – more plutonium-239. This is possible because the reaction converts both uranium-238 in the fuel mix as well as a blanket of depleted uranium surrounding the core into plutonium.

questions.question: Which one of the following is used as moderator in a nuclear reactor ?
questions.explanation: Heavy water (D2 O), also called deuterium oxide, contains a larger than normal amount of the hydrogen isotope deuterium. It is used as moderator in the reactor to slow down the neutrons produced in fission so that the chain reaction can be sustained. Many reactors also use Light water or normal water (H2 O), Graphite or Beryllium oxide as moderator. In India, mainly heavy water is used as moderator in nuclear reactors. * Graphite is used in the nuclear reactor as [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2015] - Moderator

Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen which comprises both a neutron and a proton. Deuterium or heavy hydrogen reacts with oxygen to form deuterium oxide (D2 O), also known as heavy water. questions.explanation: The first mouse prototype was invented by Dr. Douglas Engelbart. It was built in 1964. The original mouse was made of wood, with two metal wheels and a bottom. The mouse was first made public in 1968 at the Fall Joint Computer Conference.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: After the double click of the mouse, the information goes to –
questions.explanation: A double-click is an act of pressing a computer mouse button twice quickly without moving the mouse. We can communicate commands to the computer (CPU) by pressing a button on top of the mouse.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In which port do you plug-in the cable of your keyboard?
questions.explanation: USB (Universal Serial Bus) was designed to standardize the connection of computer peripherals (including keyboards, digital cameras, printers, portable media players, disk drives etc.) to personal computers, both to communicate and to supply electric power.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following groups have only input devices?
questions.explanation: Input devices send data to a computer. A mouse, keyboard, and scanner all do this. Output devices receive data from a computer. Printers, projectors, and monitors all display or present data.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Internet system uses which of the following topologies?
questions.explanation: Tree topology is a 'hybrid' topology that combines characteristics of linear bus and star topologies. The internet is the best example of largest hybrid topology. Tree topology is a good choice for a large computer network as the tree topology 'divides' the whole network into parts, that are more easily manageable.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The internet works on :
questions.explanation: Packet switching is a digital networking communication method that groups all the transmitted data into suitably sized blocks called packets, which are transmitted via a medium. The best known use of packet switching is the internet and most local area networks.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The first railway station in the country to provide Google's free public Wi-Fi service is :
questions.explanation: On September 12, 2015, the Indian Railways announced its partnership with the tech giant Google to provide free Wi-Fi services to 400 railway stations across the country. In January 2016, Mumbai Central Railway Station became the first railway station in India to have Wi-Fi facility.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is not true about Li-Fi?

options.a: The full form of Li-Fi is 'Light Fidelity'
options.b: The successful test of Li-Fi in India was done by Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on 29th January, 2018
options.c: Li-Fi can send 10 GB/sec. data up to 1 km circumference
options.d: It is operated by optical fibre network

questions.answer_text: The successful test of Li-Fi in India was done by Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on 29th January, 2018
questions.explanation: Li-Fi technique was proposed by German Physicist - Harald Hass in 2011. The full form of Li-Fi is Light Fidelity. The country's Information Technology Ministry (not Information and Broadcasting Ministry) has announced the successful testing of Li-Fi - a wireless communication technology - in a pilot jointly conducted with the Indian Institute of Technology - Madras and lighting company Philips India on 29th January, 2018. Li-Fi aims to replace Wi-Fi by using lights to transmit internet signals. So, it does not need optical fibre network. Thus, in this question, both (b) and (d) options are not true. According to a report in Economic Times, the ministry tested the technology using LED bulbs and light spectrum to transmit data. Li-Fi can touch as much as 10 GB per second data over 1 km of radius.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The computer system which links and stores information among different countries in the world through a satellite is known as –
questions.explanation: Internet is the largest satellite-based communication network of the world. It links and stores information among different countries in the world through satellite and cables.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The layer between Physical and Network layer is known as?
questions.explanation: The Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model has been an essential element of computer network design since its ratification in 1984. The OSI model divides the complex task of computer-to-computer communications, traditionally called internetworking into a series of stages known as layers. The ISO-OSI model consists of seven-layer architecture. The Physical layer or layer 1 is the first (lowest) layer. The data link layer or layer 2 is the second layer and the network layer is layer 3. So, it is clear that data link layer exists between physical and network layer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Talaash is :

options.c: a multimedia portal on Internet and an optical character recognition (OCR) software in Devanagari developed by C-DAC.
options.d: a low-cost PC-based super computing platform

questions.answer_text: a multimedia portal on Internet and an optical character recognition (OCR) software in Devanagari developed by C-DAC.
questions.explanation: Talaash is a multimedia portal on the internet and also an optical character recognition (OCR) software which is operated by C-DAC in Devanagari.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: To safeguard against cyber attacks and threats of data theft, the ‘Centre for Development of Advanced Computing’ has developed a new software called –
questions.explanation: Software NAYAN was developed by C-DAC to safeguard against cyber attacks and threats of data theft.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: First indigenously developed Indian supercomputer is named as-
questions.explanation: First indigenously developed Indian supercomputer is named as Param-8000. It was developed by the government-run Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) in 1991. All the chips and other elements that were used in the making of PARAM were bought from the open domestic market.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs is not matched ?
questions.explanation: PARAM is a series of supercomputers designed and assembled by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Pune. It was the first supercomputer developed by India. Y2K is related with a computer, arthritis with uric acid and noise pollution is with decibel.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is a supercomputer project developed by Bhabha Atomic Research Centre ?
questions.explanation: Computer division of BARC had started development of supercomputers under the ANUPAM project in 1991, based on parallel processing techniques. The first supercomputer which was based on this parallel processing technique was 'Anupam' 860/4 using 4 Intel 860 microprocessor base boards as compute nodes. It was developed by Bhabha Atomic Research Centre for their internal work /usages.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The world’s fastest computer has been able to perform (as of Dec. 1996) :
questions.explanation: According to the situation of 1996, world fastest computer was ASCI Red, whose linpack performance was greater than 1 Teraflop/s (1012 operations per second). But now according to the latest data (November, 2024), fastest supercomputer (El Capitan) which is made by U.S., has performance speed (Rmax) of 1742.00 Petaflop/s.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The fastest computer in the world is –
questions.explanation: During the period of Question (2008), Tianhe-1A was considered as the fastest computer, while at present (As per November, 2024 list of Top 500 Supercomputers) El Capitan of U.S. is the fastest computer in the world.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Supercomputer ‘Magic Cube’ inaugurated recently has been prepared by which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: Supercomputer ‘Magic Cube’ has been made by China to know the earth’s future and calculate the potential changes to the climate and biological systems. Chinese scientists hope to calculate almost everything in natural earth systems from the formation of clouds to changes in climate in hundreds or thousands of years from now.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Y2K problem relates to :

options.a: Finding out a solution to control computer virus.
options.b: To establish uniformity with the computers operating all over the world.
options.c: To find out a suitable replacement when the last two digits of the year become zero.
options.d: To make drastic change in the working of computers after an experience of sixty years experience.

questions.answer_text: To find out a suitable replacement when the last two digits of the year become zero.
questions.explanation: Y2K bug also called Year 2000 bug or Millennium Bug, relates to a problem in the coding of computerized systems that was projected to create havoc in computer and computer networks around the world at the beginning of the year 2000 (in metric measurements K stands for thousand). To find out another way for this was really very expensive. It is called Y2K problem.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following would be the smallest and fastest computer imitating brain working –
questions.explanation: Researchers of Oxford University have been successfully invented 10 billion quantum entanglement in silicon. Entanglement is those pair of equipment which are used to develop a quantum computer. A superfast quantum computer based on qubits or quantum bits can give lots of possible answers to a single question. The traditional computer is generally based on the binary switch or decibel.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following laser ray is used in laser printers?
questions.explanation: Semiconductor laser are solid lasers which are used in laser printers and CD/DVD. It works as a light emitting device. An Excimer laser or Exciplex laser is a form of an ultraviolet laser which is commonly used in the production of microelectronic devices and eye surgery. A gas laser is mainly used to make hologram and also used to read the barcode printed on the various products. The dye laser is mainly used in astronomy and spectroscopy.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Daisy wheel printer is a type of –
questions.explanation: A daisy wheel printer is an early type of impact printer invented in 1969 by David S. Lee at Diablo Data Systems. Impact printers rely on a forcible impact to transfer ink to the media. Dot matrix printers are also categorized as an impact printer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The full form of www is –
questions.explanation: The full form of www is World Wide Web. * Who, is considered as the inventor of the World Wide Web (www)? [U.P.P.C.S (Pre) 2011] - Tim Berners-Lee

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: 'Bluetooth' technology allows –

options.a: Signal transmission on mobile phones only
options.b: Landline phone to mobile phone communication

questions.explanation: The Bluetooth technology was developed in 1994 by Jaap Haartsen. Through this technology mobile phones, laptops, calculators, and digital cameras are connected and share information and data by using radio waves.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is not infotech terminology –

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is not an infotech terminology?
questions.explanation: Among the given options, Pinaka is not related to infotech terminology. It is a multiple rocket launcher produced in India and developed by the Defence Research and Development Organization (DRDO) for the Indian Army.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is a part of Infotech terminology?
questions.explanation: In information technology, a protocol is the special set of rules, used by telecommunication connection when they communicate. A login is a set of credentials used to access to an area that requires proper authorization. Archie is a program that allows you to search the files of all the Internet FTP servers that offer anonymous FTP (File Transfer Protocol).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A set of rules that governs data communication is called:
questions.explanation: A protocol is a set of rules that governs data communication. It represents an agreement between the communicating devices. Without a protocol, two devices may be connected but not communicating with each other.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Computer virus is a –
questions.explanation: A computer virus is a destructive software program or piece of code that is loaded onto your computer without your knowledge and runs against your wishes. Viruses can also replicate themselves. All computer viruses are man-made. A simple virus that can make a copy of itself over and over again is relatively easy to produce.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following expresses error in computer data –
questions.explanation: A software bug is an error, flaw, failure or fault in a computer program or system that causes it to produce an incorrect or unexpected result or to behave in an unintended way. Most bugs arise from mistakes and errors made by people either in program's source code or its design.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: ‘Stuxnet’ worm detected in the computers of Iran is –

options.a: A Hardware to speed up internet working.
options.b: A malicious program to sabotage nuclear centrifuges.

questions.answer_text: A malicious program to sabotage nuclear centrifuges.
questions.explanation: Stuxnet is a computer worm that targets industrial control systems which are used to monitor and control large-scale industrial facilities like power plants, dams, waste processing systems and similar operations. Stuxnet worm was detected in the computers of Bushehr nuclear power plant Iran. This worm is really very deadly for the plants that are controlled by computers.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The memory of the computer is measured by –
questions.explanation: The main function of the computer memory is to store data and information. Bit or binary digit is the smallest unit of computer memory. All computers work on a binary numbering system, i.e. they process data in ones and zeros. This 1 or 0 level of storage is called a bit.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The length of a word in computers is measured by –
questions.explanation: The length of a word in computers is measured in bits. 8 Bits = 1 Byte 1024 Bytes = 1 Kilobyte 1024 kilobytes = 1 Megabyte

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: One byte equals to how many bits ?
questions.explanation: The computer memory is expressed in kilobytes or megabytes or gigabytes. 1 byte equals to 8 binary digits (bits). 1 kilobyte = 1024 bytes 1 megabyte = 1024 kilobytes 1 gigabyte = 1024 megabytes 1 terabyte = 1024 gigabytes * One kilobyte is equal to [U.P.P.C.S. (R.I.) 2014; U.P. Lower Sub. (Mains) 2015; U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2017] - 1024 bytes * Which relation is not correct? [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2021] - 1 Gigabyte = 1024 Kilobytes

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The term bit is the short form of
questions.explanation: A bit (short for binary digit) is the smallest unit of data in a computer. A bit has a single binary value, either 0 or 1.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a self complementing code ?
questions.explanation: If a code is constructed in such a way that when we replace 1 by 0 and 0 by 1 in the 4-bit code representation of a digit, it is called a self-complementing code. For example, the (2421) and the (5211) codes are self- complementing. A necessary condition for a self-complementing weighted code is that the sum of its weights be 9. Digit 8421 and 5421 codes are not self complimenting codes whereas 5211, 2421, 3321, 4311 are self complimenting.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Computer hardware, which can store a very large quantity of data, is called :
questions.explanation: Magnetic tape and magnetic disk both are capable of storing a very large quantity of data. However, in comparison to magnetic tape, a magnetic disk is able to store more data. Before the invention of hard disk, magnetic tapes were widely used.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Index hole is related to –
questions.explanation: A small index hole in the floppy disk is used for referencing the beginning point of the stored data.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: IRQ 6 is commonly assigned to :
questions.explanation: By default, IRQ 6 is assigned to the Floppy Drive Controller which is a standard function integrated on to most mother-boards.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A Program that controls a computer's basic functions?
questions.explanation: Operating systems are essential parts of any computer system and are indispensable in several modern electronic devices. Apart from doing the basic functions such as memory management, device management, process management etc., operating systems are now having several other capabilities such as watching movies, listening audios, web browsing etc.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The most important part of a computer is –
questions.explanation: Central Processing Unit (C.P.U.) is the most important part of a computer. Here computer analyzes the received information or data. * What is correct in respect to CPU? [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2021] - CPU – refers to Central Processing Unit

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A word document, video or MP3 is a –
questions.explanation: Computer files have two parts to their names - a descriptive name and a file extension. A file extension is part of the file name and uniquely identifies the type of the file, also referred as format of the file. For example .doc is a file created by Microsoft Word. Similarly .mp3 is a music file that can be opened by any application which handles MP3 files.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is the main electronic component of the third generation computer?
questions.explanation: Integrated circuits (ICs) are used in the third generation computers. This circuit was invented by Jack Kilby and Robert Noyce. The electronic circuit formed by constructing electronic components like transistor, resistor, and capacitor on a small piece of semiconducting material is called integrated circuit.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Miniaturization of present day computers has been possible due to the use of –
questions.explanation: Integrated circuit is a set of electronic circuits on one small plate of semiconductor material normally silicon. After its invention in 1958, it is used in place of transistors in the computer and hence we can say that the miniaturization of present day computers has been possible due to these integrated circuit units.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the material used in the manufacturing of IC chips in computers?
questions.explanation: Silicon is the material used in the manufacturing of IC chips in computers. It is a semiconductor and in 1958 J.S. Kilby developed a complete integrated circuit in the form of a chip, which is called IC-chip.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is the newest substance being used in the production of computer chips ?
questions.explanation: Silicon is the newest substance being used in the production of computer chips, also called as integrated chips or IC chips. These chips can be used to store more data in a small space.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: ICs are classified on the basis of :
questions.explanation: ICs can be classified on the basis of their chip size as given below : Small Scale Integration (SSI) - 3 to 30 transistors/chips Medium Scale Integration (MSI) - 30 to 300 transistors/chips Large Scale Integration (LSI) - 300 to 3,000 transistors/chip Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) - more than 3000 transistors/chip.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.exam_tag: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2002; U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2007; U.P. ; Lower Sub. (Mains) 2015; U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) ; 2013; U.P.U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2002
questions.question: The device by which data are transferred by telephone with the help of binary signals is –
questions.explanation: Modem, short for Modulator/Demodulator, is a hardware device that allows a computer to send and receive information over telephone lines by converting digital signal into an analog signal and analog signal into digital signal. Thus, modem performs modulation and demodulation and it is required for sending and receiving data between computers around the world through telephone lines.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The content of computer memory which is non-volatile, even when the power goes off is:
questions.explanation: ROM (Read-Only Memory) is non-volatile, meaning it retains its contents even when the power is turned off. This is why it’s used to store essential instructions that the computer needs to start up and operate correctly. In contrast, RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile. Its contents are lost when the power is turned off.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In a computer, the permanent memory is called –
questions.explanation: ROM is considered as the permanent memory of computer. Data or information in ROM is not destroyed or erased even after the computer is turned off.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In computer terminology, RAM stands for –
questions.explanation: RAM is an acronym for random-access memory. It is considered as temporary memory and works only when the computer is functioning. Once the computer is switched off, all the data which is stored in RAM are lost or erased.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the fastest memory ?
questions.explanation: Cache memory, also called as CPU memory, is random-access memory (RAM) that a computer microprocessor can access more quickly than it can access regular RAM. The Cache has the shortest access time or latency of all the levels of the storage system and the highest bandwidth.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is not correct statement about 'Flash memory' ?

options.a: It is used for information storage in devices like digital cameras, laptops etc.
options.b: It can operate in extended temperature range of - 400 C to + 85°C.
options.c: It is cheaper than the normal mechanical disk drives.

questions.answer_text: It is cheaper than the normal mechanical disk drives.
questions.explanation: 'Flash memory' which is used in computers and other digital bodies or devices is a type of memory that persists even when the power is off. Pen drive, digital camera, and memory card are the examples of flash memory. In comparison to the hard drive, a flash memory is much energy efficient. But if we compare in the terms of per unit storage of flash drive, it is expensive than normal hard drive.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is scientific computer language ?
questions.explanation: FORTRAN is derived from 'Formula Translation'. This high level scientific computer language was developed by IBM.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: BASIC is a ......language ?
questions.explanation: Procedural programming languages include C, FORTRAN, PASCAL, BASIC etc.

options.a: Convert basic language into machine language

options.d: Convert assembly language into high level language.

questions.answer_text: Convert assembly language into machine language
questions.explanation: The main work of assembler is to convert assembly language into machine language.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which infotech terminology used to find out the User’s E-mail address ?
questions.explanation: 'Finger' protocol is used to find out the user's E-mail address.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Bibliometry is :
questions.explanation: Bibliometry is an Information Management Tool. Bibliometry is a quantitative statistical technique to measure levels of production and dissemination of knowledge, as well as a useful tool to track the development of an scientific area.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The ability of an operating system to run more than one application at a time is called :
questions.explanation: In computing, multitasking is a concept of performing multiple tasks over a certain period of time by executing them concurrently.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What kind of digital files can be attached to the e-mail?
questions.explanation: Electronic mail, or e-mail, is a method of exchanging digital messages between people using digital devices such as computers, tablets, and mobile phones. An e-mail attachment is a digital file sent along with an e-mail message. The files that can be attached to the email include documents, text files, music, audio files, video files, photos etc. * Which types of files can be sent as an e-mail attachment? [U.P. Lower Sub. (Mains) 2015] - All types of file

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The full form of SIM is :
questions.explanation: The full form of SIM is Subscriber Identity Module. It is a small card that contains a mobile network subscriber’s account information. This allows the phone using the card to attach to a mobile network. About half the size of a typical stamp, the SIM card is most commonly associated with GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) and UMTS (Universal Mobile Telecommunication System) handsets.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: ICT stands for :
questions.explanation: ICT stands for Information and Communications Technology. ICT refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the internet, wireless networks, cellphones and other communication mediums.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A.T.M. means –
questions.explanation: ATM is short for Automated Teller Machine. Basically, the ATM is used to perform banking transactions like withdrawal of money and to view bank statement.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: 'Sky Drive' is the name of Cloud Computing Service of which one of the following companies ?
questions.explanation: SkyDrive is a personal cloud storage service from Microsoft that enables customers to store, synchronize and access their files across Windows PC, macOS X computers and laptops as well as mobile devices like smartphones and tablets including Windows Phone 7 and 8 devices and Apple IOS-powered iPhones and iPads. SkyDrive has been changed to One Drive now.

questions.question: 'Davinci+' and 'veritas' – two new mission announced by NASA, are related to :
questions.explanation: 'veritas' and 'davinci+' will be NASA's first missions to Venus since the 1990s. veritas is tentatively scheduled to launch in December 2027, and would begin orbiting Venus in July 2028 (DAVINCI +'s launch is targeted for 2029). These missions are Part of NASA's Discovery Programme. The VERITAS (Venus Emissivity, Radio Science, InSAR, Topography, and Spectroscopy) mission will map the surface of the planet, study its geology, and hunt for volcanic activity. VERITAS – which means truth in Latin – will help scientists learn the facts about how Venus became a sulfurous inferno, while Earth evolved to become home to an abundance of life. The DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) with its atmospher-ic probe, called Plus, will study the dense atmosphere of Venus to understand the trigger and evolution of the runaway greenhouse effect active on the planet.

questions.question: The 'NISAR satellite' is jointly developed by which of the following organizations?
questions.explanation: nisar (nasa-isro synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite is a joint Earth-observing mission between NASA and the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) with the goal to make global measurements of the causes and consequences of land surface changes using advanced radar imaging. In 2014, NASA and ISRO signed a partnership to collaborate on and launch NISAR. The mission is targeted to launch in 2024. NISAR will be the first satellite mission to use two different radar frequencies (L-band and S-band) to measure changes in our planet's surface less than a centimeter across. NASA is providing the mission's L-band synthetic aperture radar, a high-rate communication subsystem for science data, GPS receivers, a solid-state recorder and payload data subsystem. ISRO is providing the spacecraft bus, the S-band radar, the launch vehicle and associated launch services.

questions.question: Assertion (A): A space shuttle loses radio contact with ground station for a while during landing on the Earth. Reason (R) : As a space shuttle enters Earth’s atmosphere, the shuttle’s surface temperature increases which ionize the surrounding air. In the context of the above statements, which of the following is correct :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: When a spacecraft re-entered in the Earth's atmosphere, it experiences air drag creating friction. This results in an increase of shuttle's temperature and ionizes the surrounding air. These ionized particles disturbs the radio signals and space shuttle loses radio contact with ground station for a while during landing on the Earth.

questions.question: Given below are two statements, in which one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : Roscosmos's Luna-25 mission to moon was aimed at ensuring guaranteed access to moon. Reason (R) : Russia and China together are leading International Lunar Research Station (ILRS) against U.S. led Artemis Accord. Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code :

options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
options.d: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not correct

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Luna-25 was a failed Russian lunar lander mission by Russian space agency Roscosmos in August, 2023 that planned to land near the lunar south pole. Luna-25 was the first in a series of Russian missions planned as part of the International Lunar Research Station (ILRS), a project initiated by China and Russia to build a base at the lunar south pole by the mid-2030s with the aim of using the rich water-ice resources there for long-term exploration and settlement. Russia and China together are leading ILRS against the U.S. led Artemis Accords. The Artemis Accords is a series of non-binding bilateral arrangements between the United States government and other world governments that elaborates on the norms expected to be followed in outer space. The accords are related to the Artemis program, an American-led effort to return humans to the Moon by 2026, with the ultimate goal of expanding space exploration to Mars and beyond. Hence, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation.

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: NASA made it clear by his experiment that gravitation is must for lighting up a candle. In the case of microgravity in the spacecraft, we are able to light up the flame but it is not possible in an actual vacuum. In fact, the flickering frequency of a flame is proportional to the square root of the acceleration due to gravity to the diameter of the candle and due to the lack of gravitational force in space, it is zero. Thus, the correct Answer is (a).

questions.question: The principle of ‘Black hole’ was enunciated by :
questions.explanation: Indian American astrophysicist Subrahmanyan Chandra-sekhar was best known for rendering the theory of 'Chandra sekhar Limit'. For this, he used Albert Einstein's special theory of relativity and the principle of quantum physics. Chandrasekhar showed that it is impossible for a white dwarf star to be stable if its mass is greater than 1.44 times that of the Sun. If such a star does not completely exhaust its thermonuclear fuel, then this limiting mass may be slightly larger. A star that ends its nuclear-burning lifetime with a mass greater than the Chandrasekhar limit must be either a Neutron star or a black hole. For this contribution in astrophysics he was awarded the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics with William A. Fowler.

questions.explanation: Black hole is actually a collapsed star. Black holes of stellar mass are expected to form when very massive stars collapse at the end of their life cycle. After a black hole has formed, it can continue to grow by absorbing mass from its surroundings. By absorbing other stars and merging with other black holes, supermassive black holes of millions of solar masses may form. A black hole is a place in space where gravity pulls so much that even light cannot get out. The gravity is so strong because matter has been squeezed into a tiny space.

questions.question: The tail of a comet always points –
questions.explanation: Comets are the small celestial objects made of ice, gas, dust, and a small amount of organic material that orbit our Sun. Radiation from the Sun pushes dust particles away from the coma (nebulous envelope around the nucleus of a comet), forming a dust tail, while charged particles from the Sun convert some of the comet's gases into ions, forming an ion tail. Since comet tails are shaped by sunlight and the solar wind, they always point away from the Sun.

questions.explanation: Jet engines and rockets work on the same principle. They produce thrust through an internal pressure difference and as explained by Newton's third law of motion, eject exhaust gases in an equal and opposite direction. The main difference between them is that a Jet gets the oxygen to burn its fuel from the air while a rocket carries its own supply of oxygen (oxidiser) and fuel in the form of liquid or solid propellants which allows it to operate in space.

Reason (R) :Supply of SBSP is 99% uninterrupted throughout the year, besides the enormity of energy availability. Select the correct answer using the codes given below : Code :

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Space-based solar power (SBSP) is a system for the collection of solar power in space for use on Earth. SBSP would differ from current solar collection methods in such a way that the means used to collect energy would reside on an orbiting satellite instead of the Earth's surface. The power is then transmitted via electromagnetic waves at 2.45 GHz to dedicated receiver stations on Earth. "Rectenna" convert the electromagnetic energy into electricity which is used in the local grid. The supply of SBSP will be 99% uninterrupted throughout the year besides the enormity. Former president Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam suggested that the space-based solar power (SBSP) should be made a national goal.

questions.explanation: The world’s most accurate atomic clock that loses just a second every 300 million years uses Strontium atoms. questions.question: The Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is based on the phenomenon of –
questions.explanation: MRI is a non-invasive medical test that physicians use to diagnose and treat medical conditions. It uses a powerful magnetic field, radio frequency pulses, and a computer to produce detailed pictures of organs, soft tissues, bone and all other internal body structures visually. The Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is based on the phenomenon of nuclear magnetic resonance.

It is a new device used in regenerative and degenerative tissue engineering and repairing. The cytotron is now being used for treating diseases like osteoarthritis and cancer.

questions.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : A solution of table salt in a glass of water is homogeneous. options.d: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct

questions.explanation: Homogeneous solutions have the same composition and properties throughout the solution. None of the components involved in the homogeneous solution can be detected or observed separately. A solution of table salt in a glass of water is an example of a homogeneous solution. A solution having different compositions and properties throughout is a heterogeneous mixture. Individual components of a heterogeneous mixture can be discreetly observed. questions.question: After cutting cucumber if salt is added, then water comes out due to :
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the process when water (or solvent) molecules move from a region (solution) of low concentration to a region(solution) of higher concentration through a semi-permeable membrane. When salt is applied to cucumber or cut onion pieces, it makes their surrounding more concentrated than the concentration of their cell sap. Then it causes the water molecules in the cells of the cucumber and the cut onion pieces to move to the surrounding through their cell membrane (which is semipermeable).

questions.question: These days yellow lamps are frequently used as street light. Which one of the following is used in these lamps :
questions.explanation: There are 2 types of street light lamps which are used by municipalities. They are sodium vapor and mercury vapor lamps. The mercury vapor lamps have usually a white ambient light and sodium vapor lamps have orange/yellow light. Compared to LPS (Low-pressure sodium) lamps, high-pressure sodium lamps tend to have a longer life, less lumen per watt efficiency and most importantly a higher colour rendering index.

questions.explanation: A sodium-vapor lamp is a gas-discharge lamp that uses sodium in an excited state to produce light. Low-pressure sodium lamps only give monochromatic yellow light and so inhibit colour vision at night and will not split through water droplets. Sodium-vapor lamps cause less light pollution than mercury-vapor lamps.

questions.explanation: Mercury is a chemical element with the symbol (Hg). Mercury is used in thermometers due to its special properties. It can measure a wide range of temperatures from -40 to 356o C and up to 570o C under pressure in a liquid state. It expands regularly in proportional to the absolute temperature changes. A heavy, silvery d-block element, mercury is the only common metal element which is found in liquid state at standard conditions for temperature and pressure. It is a metal, so it is a conductor of heat. Mercury is the poorest conductor of heat among all metals, but among the given options it is the best conductor of heat. * Which one metal is liquid at ordinary temperature? [U.P.P.C.S. questions.question: Mercury is basically used in thermometer devices because its especiality is –
questions.explanation: Mercury is easily the best liquid to use in thermometers, five important reasons are – (1) It is very reflective, so it's easy to see and to read accurately. (2) It doesn't wet the glass, so you don't get an inaccurate reading if the temperature is falling. (3) It is a metal, so it is a conductor of heat. (4) It expands evenly with the temperature with high circulation power, so a linear scale can be used with a high degree of accuracy. (5) There is a large range of temperature for which it is a liquid.

options.b: Both (A) and (R) is correct, but (R) is not the right classification of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) is correct, and (R) is right clarification of (A).
questions.explanation: Galvanization is the process of applying a protective zinc coating on steel or iron to prevent them from rusting and oxidation. The zinc forms a barrier between atmospheric oxygen and the underlying iron or steel. It does this by transferring electrons and oxidizing more quickly than iron. This rapid zinc oxidation prevents ferrous metals from rusting until the zinc has exhausted its free-electron capacity or the protective coating has worn away.

questions.explanation: Oxygen and moisture are essential in corrosion of iron metal. Iron corrosion is generally characterized by the formation of rust due to an electrochemical process in the presence of oxygen and moisture (water) in the surrounding environment. When iron reacts with water and oxygen, iron (II) hydroxide is formed. The latter further reacts with oxygen and water to form hydrated iron (III) oxide-widely known as rust.

Thermodynamically, graphite has a high melting point, modest thermal expansion, and high specific heat, making it relevant for composites and structural materials and as heat shields in certain applications, including nuclear reactors. Graphite consists of layers of carbon sheets (graphene sheets) that are only weakly bonded with each other causing great anisotropy in the material.

The two scientists of Manchester University-Andre Geim and Kostya Novoselov discovered it in 2004. The both were awarded 'Nobel Prize' in 2010 for the discovery of Graphene. They extracted Graphene from a piece of Graphite. Graphene is a bi-dimensional element and due to this quality, controlling electricity is easier in it than a tri-dimensional element. Graphene is not only very thin but also strongest among all the materials tested so far. It is almost transparent, despite, being so dense that the smallest gas molecule cannot pass through it. It can be used as 'conducting electrodes' required for touchscreens, LCDs and organic LEDs. Graphene is used in computer chips, communication devices and touchscreens etc.

options.c: Contains more dissolved minerals and salts

questions.answer_text: Contains deuterium in place of Hydrogen
questions.explanation: Heavy water (D2 O) or deuterium oxide is used as a moderator as well as a coolant in nuclear reactors because it slows down neutrons effectively and also has a low probability of absorption of neutrons. Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen which comprises both a neutron and a proton. Deuterium or heavy hydrogen reacts with oxygen to form deuterium oxide (D2 O), also known as heavy water. Normal water (H2 O) also used as a moderator as well as a coolant in nuclear reactors.
