questions.question: The process used for transforming salty water into pure water is called –
questions.explanation: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a water purification technology that uses a semipermeable membrane to remove larger particles from drinking water. It is used in desalination of sea water or salty water. The most widely used method of desalination on a large scale involves reverse osmosis. If pure water and salty water are placed on both sides of a semipermeable membrane, water will flow towards the salty water side. If a high pressure (higher than the osmotic pressure) is applied to the salty water side of the semi-permeable membrane, the water will flow in the opposite direction and pure water will be obtained. Reverse osmosis can remove many types of molecules and ions from solutions including bacteria and is used in both industrial processes and the production of potable pure water.

questions.explanation: Hydrogen gas is used in the manufacturing of vanaspati ghee. To prepare the vanaspati ghee, hydrogen gas is passed through vegetable oils under 8-10 atmospheric pressure in the presence of nickel powder (which works as catalyst) at a temperature of 150-180o C, and oil changes into vegetable ghee or solid fat known as vanaspati ghee. This process is called hydrogenation. Hydrogenation is a process in which unsaturated compounds combine with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst and in other suitable conditions and are converted into saturated compounds. * Which catalyst is used in hydrogenation of vegetable oils? [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2016] - Nickel

questions.question: Which of the following elements is not a Noble gas?
questions.explanation: The noble gases make a group of chemical elements with similar properties under standard conditions. They are all odourless, colourless, monatomic gases with very low chemical reactivity. These gases do not undergo chemical reactions under certain given conditions. The six noble gases that occur naturally are Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe) and the radioactive Radon (Rn).

questions.explanation: The deep sea divers carry cylinders which contain a mixture of oxygen and helium. The presence of helium generates less airway resistance than air and thereby requires less mechanical energy to ventilate the lungs. Helium is much less soluble in water than many other gases, such as nitrogen. The low solubility means it does not enter the blood stream even under pressure.

questions.explanation: Ammonia being a polar molecule dissolves readily in water. This is due to the hydrogen atoms of ammonia which are bonded with a highly electronegative nitrogen and the hydrogen atoms of water molecules which are bonded with the highly electronegative oxygen atom. Ammonia and water are both polar molecules and they are both capable of hydrogen bonding, so they are highly miscible.

questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide (N2 O) is also known as laughing gas. It is a colourless gas with a slight metallic odour and taste. Its inhalation leads to disorientation, euphoria, numbness, loss of coordination, dizziness and ultimately a loss of consciousness. It is also used as the anaesthetic gas. This gas is used in medical and dental procedures as a sedative. It helps to relieve anxiety before the procedure and allow the patient to relax. * Which gas is known as laughing gas? [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2023] - Nitrous oxide

options.b: Increase in the amount of nitrogen in lithosphere
options.c: The amount of nitrogen in lithosphere and in atmosphere unchanged

questions.answer_text: The amount of nitrogen in lithosphere and in atmosphere unchanged
questions.explanation: The nitrogen cycle is a process by which nitrogen is converted into its various chemical forms. This transformation can be carried out through both biological and physical processes. The nitrogen cycle includes fixation, ammonification, nitrification and denitrification. Denitrifying bacteria converts nitrate and nitrite ions into nitrogen. From discharge of this nitrogen, its amount in the lithosphere and in atmosphere remains unchanged.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following acids is used in the manu-facturing of baking powder ?
questions.explanation: Tartaric acid is used in the manufacturing of baking powder. This tartaric acid occurs naturally in many plants particularly in grapes, bananas and tamarinds. It is commonly combined with baking soda to function as a leavening agent in recipes and is one of the main acids found in wine.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Vinegar is the solution of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Acetic acid (CH3 COOH) or ethanoic acid is an organic acid, which is responsible for sour taste and the pungent smell of the vinegar. The physical and chemical properties prove that the vinegar is a solution of acetic acid. It is produced from fermentation of ethanol.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is not an explosive :
questions.explanation: Nitrochloroform, also known as chloropicrin, is a chemical compound currently used as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial, fungicide, herbicide, and insecticide. It is also used as tear gas. It was manufactured for use as poison gas in World War I. Other options are explosives.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: 'Nobel oil' is the name of which one of the following explosives?
questions.explanation: Trinitroglycerin (TNG) also known as Nobel oil, is an explosive fluid. Chemically, it is an organic nitrate compound.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: RDX was invented by
questions.explanation: RDX, the abbreviation of Research Department Explosive, is also called cyclonite. This powerful explosive was discov-ered by George Friedrich Henning of Germany and patented in 1898 but not used until World War II, when most of the warring powers introduced it. * Which one statement is correct? [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1996] - RDX is an explosive. * What is another name of RDX? [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2007] - Cyclonite

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following explosives does not contain nitroglycerine as an essential constituent ?
questions.explanation: Cordite, blasting gelatin and dynamite contain nitroglycerin as an essential constituent, while a highly explosive element is Amatol. It is composed of ammonium nitrate and TNT (Trinitrotoluene) in varying ratios.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is used in the production of explosives?
questions.explanation: Glycerol is an organic compound. Reacting with conc. HNO3 and conc. H2 SO4 , it produces nitroglycerin. Nitroglycerin is a heavy, colourless, oily, explosive liquid. It is also called trinitroglycerin (TNG), glyceryl trinitrate (GTN) or Nobel’s oil. It is mainly used in the explosives such as dynamite.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a natural fuel?
questions.explanation: The petroleum products are subject to natural fuel. They are made from the fossils buried within the earth. Other options coke and tar can be achieved by destructive distillation of coal or wood, while coal gas can be created artificially.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following fossil fuels is the cleanest fuel ?
questions.explanation: The use of natural gas in power generation provides a cleaner alternative to coal and other fossil fuels, reducing carbon and other emissions and resulting in both immediate and long-term benefits for public health and the environment.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels, including coal, oil and natural gas are currently the world’s primary energy sources. The fossil fuels formed from the organic material over the course of million of years have fuelled the global economy over the past century. Yet the fossil fuels are finite resources and they can also irreparably harm the environment.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Octane number is a measure of the quality of –
questions.explanation: The octane number of a fuel (petrol) is the measure of its antiknock quality when it is used in a spark ignition, internal combustion engine as compared to the antiknock quality of ISO-octane. The higher octane number of a fuel means the better anti-knocking capacity for that fuel.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Cetane number is used as a quality parameter mainly for which of the following?
questions.explanation: As the octane number is used to measure the ignition stability of gasoline (petrol), the cetane number is used as a quality parameter of diesel. The combustion of diesel without spark is provided by compression. Thus as soon as the diesel fuel is ignited and compressed the cetane number will be higher. This identifies the good quality of diesel.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The fuel used in a diesel engine :

options.d: Mixture of diesel, air and petrol

questions.explanation: A diesel engine is an internal combustion engine in which ignition in fuel is generated by using heat produced by compressing air in closed place. There is no carburetor in diesel engines for combustion as in petrol engines. In a diesel engine, the air inside a cylinder is compressed to such a level so that the temperature of air reaches 80o F and this temperature works as combustion in diesel engines.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In which of the following types of heat engines carburetor is used?
questions.explanation: A carburetor is a device used by an internal combustion engine to control and mix air and fuel entering the engine. While the earlier versions of carburetors used to do this merely by allowing air to pass over the fuel surface, the advanced version of carburetors dispense a metered amount of fuel into the stream of air to achieve this purpose. Since the 1990s, carburetors have been largely replaced by fuel injection for cars and trucks, however carburetors are still used by some small engines (e.g. lawnmowers, generators and concrete mixers) and motorcycles. Carburetors are only used in petrol engines. Diesel engines have always used fuel injection instead of carburetors.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following gases, released from biogas plant is used as a fuel gas?
questions.explanation: Methane is the principal gas in biogas. It is also the main component of natural gas, a fossil fuel, and can be used to replace natural gas in many applications including cooking, heating, steam production, etc.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Biogas mainly consists of –
questions.explanation: Biogas typically refers to a mixture of different gases produced by the breakdown of organic matter in the absence of oxygen. Biogas is primarily methane and carbon dioxide and may have small amounts of hydrogen sulfide, moisture and siloxanes. Biogas or gobar gas generally contains about 50%-75% Methane and about 25%-45% carbon dioxide. * The main component of Gobar Gas is [U.P.P.S.C. (GIC) 2010] - Methane

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the procedure for a biogas plant–
questions.explanation: The gobar gas formed from cattle dung and other wastes, has a lot of energy which can be stored for a biogas plant by the process of fermentation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Who among the following invented 'Gobar Gas' system?
questions.explanation: The first pilot gas plant for producing methane from cattle dung and other cellulosic organic materials was first designed by S.V. Desai and set up at the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi, during 1941-42.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The main component of Liquid Petroleum Gas (LPG) are :
questions.explanation: LPG is the abbreviation or short form for Liquefied Petroleum Gas. Like all fossil fuels, it is a non-renewable source of energy. It is extracted from crude oil and natural gas. The main composition of LPG are hydrocarbons containing three or four carbon atoms. The normal components of LPG thus are propane (C3 H8 ) and butane (C4 H10). LPG mixtures contain a little more propane in winter and a little more butane during summer but, on average, the makeup is approximately 65% butane and 35% propane. Small concentrations of other hydrocarbons like ethane may also be present. Ethyl mercaptan is normally used as a stenching agent for smell. * Indane gas is a mixture of [U.P.P.C.S (Pre) 2011] - Butane and Propane

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: CNG is –
questions.explanation: C.N.G. is the short form of Compressed Natural Gas. It is a readily available alternative to gasoline which is made by compressing natural gas to less than 1% of its volume at standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: CNG used in automobiles to check pollution mainly consists of –
questions.explanation: CNG is made by compressed natural gas which is mainly composed of methane (CH4 ). It is a mixture of hydrocarbons which is found deep inside Earth and have approx. 80% to 90% of methane. * Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is mainly composed of [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2022] - Methane

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Gasohol is a mixture of :
questions.explanation: Gasohol, a gasoline extender made from a mixture of gasoline (petrol) and ethanol (often obtained by fermenting agricultural crops). Gasohol has higher octane or anti-knock properties by which it burns more slowly, coolly and completely.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following countries has made it mandatory to blend ethanol with gasoline?
questions.explanation: Since 1976, the Brazilian Government has made it mandatory to blend ethanol with gasoline and since 2007, the legal blend is around 25% ethanol and 75% gasoline.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements : 1. Coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels. 2. Gasohol is a mixture of benzene and alcohol. 3. Geothermal energy is non-conventional energy source. 4. Gobar gas contains mainly methane. Of these statements :
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are hydrocarbons primarily coal, fuel oil or natural gas formed from the remains of dead plants and animals. Sometimes, they are known as mineral fuels. Fossil fuels are fuels formed by a natural process such as anaerobic decomposition of buried dead organisms. Ethanol fuel mixtures have "E" number which describes the percentage of ethanol fuel in the mixture by volume. E 85 is 85% denatured ethanol fuel and 15% gasoline. Low-ethanol blends from E5 to E 25 are also known as gasohol.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the by-product derived from the refining process of petroleum?
questions.explanation: Asphalt is also known as bitumen, is a sticky, black and highly viscous liquid or semi-solid form of petroleum. It may be found in natural deposits or may be refined product. The primary use of asphalt is in road construction, where it is used as the glue or binder mixed with aggregate particles to create asphalt concrete. Its other uses are for bituminous waterproofing product, including the production of roofing felt and for sealing flat roofs.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: To avoid ‘knocking’ of the engine of a car, which one of the following is used as an anti-knocking agent?
questions.explanation: Tetraethyl Lead (CH3 CH2 )4 Pb is the chief anti-knock agent for automotive gasoline or petrol. In the hot cylinder of a gasoline engine, the bonds between the lead atom and the ethyl groups are broken. Upon combustion, the lead atom forms lead oxide (PbO) which prevents fractions of the fuel mixture from burning too quickly and causing a highly undesirable engine knock. Thus, it is mixed with petrol to increase its anti-knocking rate. * Tetraethyl Lead (TEL) is added to petrol [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1996] - To increase its anti-knocking rating

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Diesel used in heavy vehicles for –

options.b: Low expense and save the fuel

questions.explanation: An internal combustion engine transforms the chemical energy in fuel to mechanical rotational energy. Diesel engine, which are in existence for over a century, are the most versatile and economical engine used in a heavy vehicle. Today's direct-injection diesel engines are more rugged, powerful, durable and reliable than gasoline engines and use fuel much more efficiently as well.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Hydrogen gas can be conveniently used as a fuel for running vehicles if it is absorbed at very low temperature by a substance only to be released at the temperature generated by the exhaust. What is that substance found in India?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen gas is absorbed by palladium hydride at very low temperature. It is used to power a range of new alternate fuel vehicles.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: ‘Hydrocarbon Vision 2025’ is associated with :

options.b: Euro I and Euro II vehicles

questions.explanation: 'Hydrocarbon Vision 2025' is associated with storage of petroleum products and focus on long-term energy security. Aims to assure energy security by achieving self-reliance through increased indigenous production and investment in equity oil abroad.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is used in preservation?
questions.explanation: The chemical formula of Sodium Benzoate is C7 H5 NaO2 . It is widely used as a food preservative, with E number E211. It is the sodium salt of benzoic acid and exists in this form when dissolved in water and its melting point is 410o C. * For the preservation of fruit juice which of the following is used? [U.P.P.S.C. (R.I.) 2014] - Sodium Benzoate

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is used in food preservation?
questions.explanation: Benzoic acid (C7 H6 O2 ) or C6 H5 COOH is the colourless crystalline solid and simple aromatic carboxylic acid. The name is derived from gas benzoin. Its salts (e.g. sodium benzoate) are used as food preservative.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Potato chips are packed in plastic bags in the atmos-phere of :
questions.explanation: Potato chips are packed in plastic bags in the atmosphere of nitrogen to protect them from being oxidized. It gives the chips a longer shelf life because bacteria, molds, etc. need oxygen to thrive, and in the absence of oxygen they cannot grow. It also keeps away moisture and keeps the chips intact during transportation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Refrigeration helps in food preservation by –

options.b: Reducing the rate of biochemical reactions
options.d: Sealing the food with a layer of ice

questions.answer_text: Reducing the rate of biochemical reactions
questions.explanation: Refrigeration preserves foods by slowing down the growth and reproduction of microorganisms or we can say that by refrigeration we can reduce the rate of biochemical reactions.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Charcoal which is used in decolouring raw sugar is :
questions.explanation: Animal charcoal also, known as bone charcoal is primarily used for filtration and decolourization. Bone charcoal is often used in sugar refining as a decolourizing and de-ashing agent.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The main component of honey is :
questions.explanation: The main components of honey are fructose - 38.2%, glucose - 31.3%, sucrose - 1.3%, maltose - 7.1% and water - 17.2%. Fructose or fruit sugar is a simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : Invert sugar is more sweet than sucrose. Reason (R) : Invert sugar is obtained by the hydrolysis of sucrose. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Invert sugar is made by splitting disaccharide sucrose into its two components monosaccharides fructose and glucose (dextrose). The conventional way to make invert sugar is by the hydrolysis of sucrose to glucose and fructose. Invert sugar is sweeter than sucrose (ordinary white sugar) due to free fructose crystals in it which is the sweetest natural sugar. Hence, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following compounds is used as a sedative?
questions.explanation: Potassium Bromide (KBr) is a salt, widely used as an anticonvulsant and a sedative in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is used as a veterinary drug, as an antiepileptic medication for dogs. It is an odourless, colourless crystals or white granular solid with a pungent bitter saline taste.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following forms an irreversible complex with a hemoglobin of the blood?

options.d: A mixture of Carbon Dioxide and Helium

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a deadly, colourless, odourless, poisonous gas. It is produced by the incomplete burning of various fuels including coal, wood, charcoal, oil, kerosene, propane and natural gas. Carboxyhemoglobin (COHb) is a stable complex of carbon monoxide that forms in red blood cells when carbon monoxide is inhaled.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following oil is an extract of clove oil?
questions.explanation: Eugenol is a colourless or light yellow oil extracted from clove oil having chemical formula C10H12O2 . It smells like cloves with spicy pungent taste.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following fruits is most suitable for jelly making?
questions.explanation: The smaller acid fruits are more suitable for jelly making since they are usually high in pectin content and acid. Guavas have high calcium and phosphorus contents. High pectin contents make guava suitable for jelly making.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Organic food is supposed to be better for us because it

options.a: Relies on chemicals to improve the flavour
options.c: Is grown in glasshouses keeping it clean of environmental pollutants.
options.d: Is grown without the use of artificial fertilizers and

questions.answer_text: Is grown without the use of artificial fertilizers and
questions.explanation: Organic food is produced by farmers who emphasize the use of renewable resources and the conservation of soil and water to enhance environmental quality for future generations. The organic food is produced without using most conventional pesticides; fertilizers made with synthetic ingredients or sewage sludge, bioengineering or ionizing radiation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Detergent easily removes oil and dirt from dirty garments. Reason (R) : Detergent increases the surface tension of water. Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true as the detergent easily removes oil and dirt from dirty garments. The surface tension of water is dramatically reduced by the addition of soap or detergent. The soap or detergent molecules tend to aggregate at the surface of the water. By this, they weaken the hydrogen bonding between water molecules, hence, surface tension reduces. Hence (A) is true, but (R) is false.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Assertion (A): Chemical fertilizers are necessary for the phosphorus need of plants. Reason (R) : One metric ton of organic manure can barely supply 2 or 3 kg of phosphorus. From the above statement, which are is correct :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The fertilizer is a substance added to soil to improve plant growth and yield. Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Potassium (N,P,K) are necessary elements of plants. Only 1.5 to 3 kg of Phosphorus is obtained from 1 metric ton of an organic manure. Thus, chemical fertilizers are necessary for the phosphorus need of plants.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The element not provided by the fertilizers is –
questions.explanation: The fertilizer is a chemical or natural substance added to the soil to increase its fertility. There are at least 16 elements essential for the growth of the plant. Carbon, Hydrogen and Oxygen are derived from carbon dioxide and water. Nitrogen, Phosphorous, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, Boron, Chlorine, Copper, Iron, Manganese, Molybdenum and Zinc are normally derived from the soil in the form of inorganic salts.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following fertilizers leaves maximum acidity in the soil ?
questions.explanation: The soil acidic causes a reduction in the yields of acid-sensitive crops. The acidic soils are readily identified by a soil test showing a low pH value. The soil reaction is alkaline when the pH value is above 7, neutral at 7 and acidic below 7. The extensive use of ammonium sulphate is not recommended on acidic soils because of its greater acidifying properties compared to other nitrogen fertilizers.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Urea is
questions.explanation: Urea is an organic compound whose chemical formula is CO(NH2 )2 . Nearly 46.7% of nitrogen in the urea is present in the form of amide. In the field of organic chemicals it is also called carbamide. * The percentage of nitrogen in urea is [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2009] - 47% * Which form of nitrogen is available in urea [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl.) (Mains) 2008] - Amide

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following chemical fertilizers is relatively more soluble in water at 20o C?
questions.explanation: Urea is an organic compound that is only stable in an acidic environment. It is named after the Greek word 'Oura' meaning urine. Urea is very easily soluble in water as compared to other fertilizers.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How much amount of urea will be required for supplying 1 kg of nitrogen?
questions.explanation: We know that amount of nitrogen in urea = about 46% ∴ Urea required for supplying 46 gm of nitrogen = 100 gm ∴ Urea required for supplying 1000 gm (1 kg) of nitrogen = 100 46 ×1000 = 2174 gm = 2.2 kg (approx.) Hence, about 2.2 kg of urea will be required for supplying 1 kg of nitrogen.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What percentage of phosphorus (P2 O5 ) and Nitrogen (N) is present in DAP ?
questions.explanation: The Diammonium Phosphate (DAP) is used as a fertilizer. Its formula is (NH4 ) 2 HPO4 . The average pH in solution is 7.5–8. The typical formulation is 18% N and 46% P2 O5 .

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The most popular fertilizer for foliar application is –
questions.explanation: The foliar fertilization means applying nutrients to plant leaves or needles. Urea is commonly used for foliar fertilization because of its high solubility and its rapid and effective absorption by leaves.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following assertion and reason and select the correct answer from the code given below. Assertion (A) : Ozone kills microorganism in water. Reason (R) : Ozone is not radioactive. Codes :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Ozone is made up of three oxygen atoms (O3 ) having a 'free radical' of oxygen. It will readily give up one atom of oxygen providing a powerful oxidizing agent which is toxic to most waterborne organisms such as bacteria, mold and yeast spores, viruses or harmful protozoans that form cysts. Ozone is not radioactive. Thus, Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used in fire alarm?
questions.explanation: The photocell is used in fire alarm. A photocell is a technological application of the photoelectric effect. A photocell is a resistor that changes resistance depending on the amount of light incident on it. It operates on semiconductor photoconductivity - the energy of light photons hitting the semiconductor frees electron to flow, decreasing the resistance. Photocell fire alarm device projects a continuous, focused beam of light onto a mirror. If nothing interferes with the beam en route and back, the sensor perceives no obstruction. But when a small amount of smoke enters the chamber, the light is refracted slightly, causing an alarm to sound.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following compounds is used to make fireproof clothing?
questions.explanation: Aluminium sulphate is used to prepare fireproof clothes.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used as a mosquito repellent?
questions.explanation: Pyrethrum is a natural botanical insecticide. It has potent insecticidal activity by targeting the nervous systems of insects which affects the nervous system of mosquitoes and repels them.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Pyrethrin used in mosquito coil is obtained from –
questions.explanation: Pyrethrins are a class of organic compounds normally derived from Chrysanthemum cinerariifolium, a seed plant that has potent insecticidal activity by targeting the nervous system of insects.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is used as rat poison ?
questions.explanation: Potassium cyanide (KCN) and zinc phosphide which are highly toxic chemicals, used as a rodenticide - a poison to kill the mouse.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Aluminium Phosphide is used as –
questions.explanation: Aluminium Phosphide is highly toxic inorganic compound. It is a cheap, easily available pesticide which causes lethal poisoning by liberation of phosphine gas. It is also used as fumigant for preservation of cereals and as rodenticide.

Tiny particles of silver iodide are sprayed on a cloud from an aeroplane. Sometimes, solid carbon dioxide (called dry ice) is used. The particles attract water droplets from the cloud. questions.explanation: The compound Zinc Oxide (ZnO) is called philosopher’s wool. Alchemists, as part of their rituals, would burn zinc in air and collect the residue, which formed into white woolly tufts. They called it lana philosophica in Latin, meaning philosopher's wool. Zinc oxide has many uses such as white pigment in paints, component in zinc ointment for treating skin diseases, material in sun screens and sun lotions, in rubber manufacture and in photocopying products.

questions.explanation: The main attribute common to all lightning rods is that they are all made of conductive materials such as copper and aluminium. Copper and its alloys are the most common materials used in lightning protection in buildings and houses. Haemoglobin in the blood carries oxygen from the respiratory organs (lungs or gills) to the rest of the body. Its molecule comprises four subunits, each containing an iron atom bound to a haem group. Lead-acid batteries, also known as lead storage batteries provide high current in short period of time, making them essential for vehicles. Silver Bromide is used in photography.

It is kept under the oil because it might react with air. Boric acid is a weak monobasic Lewis acid of boron often used as an antiseptic, insecticide, flame retardant etc. German silver is a copper alloy with nickel and often zinc. The usual formulation is 60% copper, 20% nickel and 20% zinc. Nickel silver is named for its silvery appearance, but it contains no elemental silver unless plated.

questions.question: Which chemical acts as a reclamation agent for alkaline soil?
questions.explanation: The term 'alkali soil' is used to designate land that is saline and has an excess of absorbed sodium carbonate and sodium chloride. An excess of sodium chloride gives a hard firm surface crust with cubical salt crystals. Alkali salts in the soil also affect the plant growth by reducing the size of leaves, plant roots remain superficial, bark of stem turns brown or black. Gypsum is calcium sulphate (CaSO4 . 2H2 O) that has no direct effect on soil pH. The main use of Gypsum is the reclamation of highly alkaline soil. Gypsum dissolves to release calcium which replaces sodium and makes the soil fertile.

options.d: Telephone was invented by Graham Bell.

questions.answer_text: The breaking apart of the nucleus of an atom is called fusion.
questions.explanation: Nuclear fusion is an atomic reaction in which multiple atoms combine to create a single, more massive atom. The resulting atom has a slightly smaller mass than the sum of the masses of the original atoms. Nuclear fission is a reaction in which a large nuclei break apart into smaller nuclei, releasing a great amount of energy. In this way statement (b) is wrong, while other statements are correct.

questions.explanation: Primitive Earth's atmosphere was rich in methane, ammonia, water vapour, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, nitrogen, hydrogen, neon etc. It was a reducing atmosphere, with no free oxygen. questions.explanation: Blue-green algae is the oldest organism on Earth. They obtain their energy through photosynthesis. They are also known as Cyanobacteria. By producing gaseous oxygen as a by-product of photosynthesis, they played a greater role in dramatically changing life forms on Earth by stimulating biodiversity.

According to him, new species are not formed by continuous variations but by the sudden appearance of variations, which he named as mutations. He stated that mutations are heritable and persist in successive generations.

questions.question: Assertion (A) : Some bacteria can synthesize their own food. Reason (R) : These bacteria have green matter called chloroplasts. Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Bacteria have a wide range of diets. Some are heterotrophs and others are autotrophs. Most heterotrophic bacteria are saprobes (they absorb dead organic material like rotting flesh). Some of these parasitic bacteria kill their host while others help their host. Autotrophic bacteria make their own food, either by photosynthesis (which uses sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food) or by chemosynthesis (which uses carbon dioxide, methane and chemicals like ammonia, hydrogen sulphide to make food). Phototrophic bacteria do not have chloroplasts. Bacteriochlorophylls are photosynthetic pigments that occur in various phototrophic bacteria.

options.b: They are on the borderline of plants and animals
options.c: They are on the borderline of flowering and non-flowering plants

questions.explanation: Bacteria are single-celled microbes. They are unicellular organisms consists of prokaryotic cell. Their cell structure is simpler than that of other organisms as there is no nucleus or membrane bound organelles. Bacteria are universal, can be found everywhere. There are some harmful bacteria that can cause illness and disease. There are other bacteria that are essential for us to survive. Bacteria in the digestive system also supply needed vitamins like biotin and vitamin K and are our primary source for some of these nutrients.

The four extant species, together with the Platypus are the only surviving members of that order and are the only living mammals that lay eggs. Their diet consists of ants and termites but they are not closely related with the true anteaters of America. They live in Australia and New Guinea.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms has white blood?
questions.explanation: Cockroaches have white or colourless blood because they lack hemoglobin in their blood. Cockroaches do not use hemoglobin to carry oxygen. In fact their bloodstream is not used to carry oxygen either. They use a system of tubes called tracheae to bring the oxygen and remove carbon dioxide from their tissues.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The silk produced by spiders is called :
questions.explanation: Spider silk is protein fiber spun by spiders. It is also known as 'Gossamer silk'. Spider silk is an extremely strong material. It is one of the most miraculous natural substances on Earth. Most building materials are either strong or elastic, but spider silk is both. It has often been described as stronger than steel (which is not quite accurate, but close).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is not obtained from insects?
questions.explanation: Among the given options silk, lac and honey are obtained from insects, while pearls are produced within the soft tissue of a living shelled mollusk or another animal such as fossil conulariids. The most valuable pearls occur spontaneously in the wild (natural pearls which are rare), while cultured or farmed pearls are obtained from bivalve mollusks, such as pearl oysters (Pinctada) and freshwater mussels.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about mosquitoes : 1. Only males suck blood 2. Only females suck blood 3. Females suck plant juices 4. Males have bigger wings than females 5. Females have bigger wings than males Of these :
questions.explanation: Only female mosquitoes suck the blood of warm-blooded vertebrate birds and mammals and live on them as an ectoparasite. The male mosquitoes do not suck blood, they survive by feeding on flowers and fruit juices. Occasionally, females may also suck juices. Generally, female mosquitoes are larger than male mosquitoes. That is why option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Desert dwelling animals are called -
questions.explanation: Xericoles are animals adapted to survive in deserts with little water and extreme temperatures.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following animals can live for the longest duration without drinking water?
questions.explanation: Among the given animals, Kangaroo rat can live for the longest duration without drinking water. The Kangaroo rat is a rodent native to the desert areas of North America. The Kangaroo rat adapted to live in the desert climate because it produces the most concentrated urine in all mammals. Their kidneys concentrate the urine so much that it becomes almost solid. * Which animal excretes solid urine? [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2017] - Kangaroo rat

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Poisonous fangs of a snake are modified form of :
questions.explanation: Poisonous fangs of a snake are modified form of maxillary teeth. There are 1-3 pairs (usually 1 pair) of long, curved, sharp and pointed maxillary teeth attached to the poison glands of the upper jaw of a snake.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Pitcher plants or Nepenthes are able to synthesize their food by the process of photosynthesis, hence they are autotrophs. Usually, they grow on soils deficient in nitrogenous compounds and fulfill their required nitrogen by digesting insects. Other options are correctly matched.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Nepenthes are not hydrophytes. They are tropical pitcher plants and a genus of carnivorous plant. Other pairs are correctly matched.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an insectivorous plant?
questions.explanation: Nepenthes are insectivorous pitcher plant. Nepenthes species are perennial herbaceous plants and frequently grow in very acidic soil, though some are epiphytes. All the species are carnivorous plants that capture insects and other prey by means of modified pitcher-shaped leaves that function as passive pitfall traps.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Nepenthes khasiana a rare and endangered plant is found in –
questions.explanation: Nepenthes khasiana is India's only pitcher plant and is named after the Khasi Hill region of Meghalaya. They are mostly found in Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills region of Meghalaya.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The type of fruit in which lychee can be placed in –
questions.explanation: Lychee is a juicy fruit belonging to the soapberry family. The fruit grows on an evergreen tree, with pinnate leaves. It is a drupe (like a plum, a cherry, or a mango), externally covered by a pink-red rough textured rind, easily removable.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Turmeric is obtained from which part of the plant :
questions.explanation: Turmeric is obtained from the modified stem (rhizome) of the plant. It is a member of the curcuma botanical group, which is part of a ginger family of herbs, the Zingiberaceae. Its botanical name is Curcuma longa. All curcumas are perennial plants native to southern Asia. They grow in warm humid climates and thrive only in temperatures above 60o F (29.8o C). India, Sri Lanka, Fiji and Queensland (Australia) all have the climate, which is conducive to grow turmeric.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Turmeric is an example of underground stem, known as :
questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following underground produced vegetables is a modified root ?
questions.explanation: The sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is a dicotyledonous plant that belongs to the family Convolvulaceae. Sweet potato is a modified root cultivated by vegetative propagation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The storage organ of which of the following plants is not a stem ?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane, potato, and ginger are modified stems i.e., their storage organ is stem, while the storage organ of sweet potato is root. It is developed by radicle.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a stem?
questions.explanation: Among the given options turnip, carrot and sweet potato are modified roots while ginger is a modified stem.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In the following pairs of plants and their edible parts, which pair is not correctly matched ?
questions.explanation: The edible part of the potato is tuber (modified stem), not root. Thus, option (c) is not correctly matched. Other options are correctly matched. * Which part of potato is edible? [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Mains) 2013] - Stem

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: 'Mycorrhiza' is a symbiotic association between :
questions.explanation: Fungi have several symbiotic (mutualistic) relationships with other organisims. In mutualism, both organisms benefitted from the relationship. Two common mutualistic relationships involving fungi are mycorrhiza and lichen. Mycorrhiza are symbiotic relationships that form between fungi and vascular plants. The fungi colonize the root system of a host plant, providing increased water and nutrient absorption capabilities while the plant provides the fungus with carbohydrates formed from photosynthesis.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Clove is a –
questions.explanation: Cloves are the aromatic closed, dried floral buds, which is used in Ayurvedic medicines, making food and as an anodyne for dental emergencies. The botanical name of clove tree is Syzygium aromaticum (Eugenia caryophyllata) which belongs to Myrtaceae family. Cloves are native of Indonesia and used as a spice in cuisines all over the world. The clove tree grows to a height ranging from generally 8-12 metres, having large oval leaves. * Which one spice is a flower bud? [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011] - Clove * 'Cloves' are [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) (Re. Exam) 2015] - Dried flowers

questions.explanation: Saffron is a spice derived from the flower of Crocus sativus, commonly known as the 'Saffron Crocus'. Saffron is obtained from the styles and stigmas of the flower of Crocus sativus. Other options are correctly matched. * Saffron is dried mixture of [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2002] - Seed forming parts of flower

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The characteristic odour of garlic is due to –
questions.explanation: Garlic is made up of sulphuric compounds (Allyl methyl sulphide) that render the pungent smell to it. It is also used as diaphoretic, diuretic, expectorant and for treating blood pressure and heart disease.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Peeling of onions causes tears as onions release –
questions.explanation: Sulfenic acid found in onions irritates lacrymal glands and produces tears in eyes.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Pungency in chillies is due to the presence of :
questions.explanation: Chillies are valued principally for their high pungency and colour. Pungency in chillies is due to the active constituent 'capsaicin', an alkaloid which is extracted from chillies and is also used in the medicine. The molecular formula of capsaicin is C18H27NO3 .

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The mulberry fruit is :
questions.explanation: The mulberry fruit is also known as the sorosis. Sorosis is a multiple fleshy fruit that is derived from the ovaries of multiple flowers. The seeds are achenes, on the outside of a fleshy fruit. Pineapple and Ficus are also the examples of Sorosis fruit.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following fibre is not a product of plant stem :
questions.explanation: The fibres of sunn, hemp, and jute are obtained from stems, while cotton is obtained from the fruit of the cotton plant, called cotton balls. Cotton fibres are classified into two types namely lint and fuzz respectively. Lint fibre is more important for the commercial purpose than fuzz fibre.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Leg-haemoglobin is found in-
questions.explanation: Leg-haemoglobin is found in root nodules of leguminous plants such as alfalfa and soyabean. It is crucial for supplying sufficient oxygen to root nodule bacteria for nitrogen fixation to occur.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which among the following is a man-made cereal?
questions.explanation: Triticale is the first man-made cereal crop. It has been obtained by crossing wheat (Triticum) with rye (Secale) in laboratories during the late 19th century in Scotland and Germany. Though the Triticale is a cross between wheat and rye, it is self-pollinating (similar to wheat) and not cross-pollinating (like rye).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Read the given statements– Assertion (A) : The root systems of desert plants are longer. Reason (R) : High temperature of soil encourages the growth of roots. Referencing above, which one is the right answer? Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Desert plants have the capability to complete their life-cycle even in a dry atmosphere. The root system of these plants become longer in search of water from the soil and their stems are small, adapted and underground sometimes. Plant varieties that have adapted by developing very long roots are collectively known as phreatophytes. * Desert plants have longer root system because [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1996] - Roots grow in search of water

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Desert plants are generally –
questions.explanation: A succulent is a plant that stores water for times when water is not available to it. Succulent plants are generally found in arid environments such as deserts and semi-deserts.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The maximum amount of water, which plants need to grow, is absorbed by the following :
questions.explanation: The maximum amount of water is absorbed by root hairs. These are outermost layer of zone of cell maturation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A hydrophyte is :
questions.explanation: Hydrophytes or aquatic plants are plants that have adapted to live in an aquatic environment. Plants growing on saline soils or water are called halophytes (salt-loving plants). They grow in saline semi-deserts, mangroove swamps, marshes and sloughs and seashores.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Plants and animals that live on land are called:
questions.explanation: Plants and animals that live on land are specifically called terrestrial habitants. The term “terrestrial” refers to land. These organisms have adaptations to survive in environments like forests, grasslands, and deserts.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is not correctly matched :
questions.explanation: Autotrophs are the producers in a food chain such as plants on land or algae in water, in contrast to heterotrophs as consumers of autotrophs. Saprotroph, a term used for organisms which obtain nutrients from dead organic matter (this term commonly applies to fungi). A herbivore is an animal anatomically and physiologically adapted to eating plant material (for example foliage) for the main component of its diet. More generally, herbivores feed on autotrophs and are known as primary consumers. Thus, option (d) is not correctly matched.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Fishes survive under the frozen lake, because-

options.b: Fishes are in hibernation under it
options.c: Water does not freeze near bottom
options.d: Ice is the conductor of heat.

questions.answer_text: Water does not freeze near bottom
questions.explanation: Lakes and rivers freeze when the outer temperature decreases below the freezing point in winter. But only the upper layer freezes in this condition. Water remains in liquid form below the upper layer. So fishes and other aquatic creatures can survive even in a frozen lake.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Redness in apple is due to –
questions.explanation: Red apples get their colour from anthocyanin pigment. * What account for the red colour of tomato? [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2016; U.P.P.C.S. (Spl.) (Mains) 2008] - Lycopene

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The yellow colour of papaya is due to -
questions.explanation: The botanical name of papaya is ‘Carica papaya’. It is rich in carotene, which is a precursor of vitamin A. The papain enzyme presented in papaya is helpful in digestion of protein. The yellow colour of papaya is due to presence of caricaxanthin.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Yeast is an example of -
questions.explanation: Yeasts, moulds (molds) and mushrooms are examples of fungi. Fungi is the plural word for fungus. Fungi lack chlorophyll and vascular bundle.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Mushroom used in for making juicy vegetable is a –
questions.explanation: Yeasts, moulds (molds) and mushrooms are examples of fungi. Fungi is the plural word for fungus. Fungi lack chlorophyll and vascular bundle.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Major component of cotton is :
questions.explanation: The chemical composition of cotton is generally as follows– Cellulose - 91.00% Water - 7.85% Protoplasm - 0.55% Elephatic elements - 0.40% Mineral salts - 0.20%

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Noscapine is obtained from :
questions.explanation: Noscapine is obtained from poppy.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Heroin is obtained from :
questions.explanation: Heroin is obtained from the opium poppy (Papaver somniferum). Opium latex contains approximately 12% of the analgesic alkaloid morphine, which is processed chemically to produce heroin and other synthetic opioids for medicinal use and for the illegal drug trade.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Opium is obtained from :
questions.explanation: Opium is the dried latex. The dried latex is obtained from the unripe fruit, by making shallow cuts.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The main constituent of opium is :
questions.explanation: Opium is a substance that is derived from the collecting and drying processes of the milky juice that comes from the unripe fruit of the poppy plant. The primary component of opium is 12% morphine which is an alkaloid that is often processed chemically to produce illegal drugs such as heroin.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How does the plant cell differ from the animal cell?
questions.explanation: A plant cell is different from animal cell mainly on the basis of the cell wall. The outer shell in a plant cell (which is made from cellulose in green plants) is known as cell wall, which is not found in the animal cell. Except this, green plastids are also found in plant cells while not in animal cells.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following organelle is called ‘Power House’ of the cell?
questions.explanation: Animal cells and plant cells both contain cell membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus. The nucleus has two major functions. It stores the cell’s hereditary material or DNA and it co-ordinates the cell’s activities within cells. The mitochondrion (plural mitochondria) is a membrane-bound organelle found in most eukaryotic cells. Mitochondria range from 0.5 to 1.0 mm in diameter. These structures are sometimes described as 'the powerhouse of the cell' as they generate energy through respiration. During cellular respiration, the initial process takes place in cytoplasm and then in mitochondria.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Plasma membrane is built up of :
questions.explanation: The cell membrane (also known as plasma membrane) is a biological membrane that separates the interior of cell from the outside environment. It is composed of two layers of phospholipids and embedded with proteins.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements is not true?

options.a: Chromosomes are composed of DNA and Protein.
options.b: Nucleus of a cell does not play a role in cellular reproduction.
options.d: Functional segment of DNA is called genes.

questions.answer_text: Nucleus of a cell does not play a role in cellular reproduction.
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains the cell’s genetic material (DNA) in the form of chromosomes. During cell division (both mitosis and meiosis), the nucleus plays a crucial role in replicating and distributing the genetic material to the daughter cells, ensuring the accurate transfer of hereditary information. Chromosomes are composed of DNA and protein. Chromosomes contain information for inheritance. Functional segments of DNA are called genes.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The classical Mendel's work on his 'laws of inheritance' was performed on the organism –
questions.explanation: Hybridization was experimented on garden pea plant first by Gregor Mendel. After studying the seven types of qualities of pea, he rendered three laws as- Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation and Law of Independent Assortment.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Genome mapping relates to :
questions.explanation: Gene mapping is the method used for determining the location of genes and relative distances between genes on a chromosome. The essence of all genome mapping is to place a collection of molecular markers onto their respective positions on the genome. Molecular markers come in all forms. Genes can be viewed as one special type of genetic markers in the construction of genome maps and mapped the same way as any other markers.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Change in the base sequence within a gene is called:
questions.explanation: A gene is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity. Change in the base sequence within a gene is called mutation. Mutation is the changing of the structure of a gene, resulting in a variant form that may be transmitted to the subsequent generations. Mutation is the ultimate source of all genetic variation, providing the raw material on which evolutionary forces such as natural selection can act.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The unit of heredity in our body is called :
questions.explanation: A gene is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity. Genes, which consists of DNA, are the genetic material and unit of heredity. In humans, genes vary in size from a few hundred DNA bases to more than 2 million bases.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which compound present in D.N.A. does not form amino acid ?
questions.explanation: Tyrosine or 4-hydroxyphenylalanine is one of the 22 amino acids that are used by cells to synthesize proteins. Its codons are UAC and UAU. It is a non-essential amino acid with a polar side group. It was first discovered in 1846 by German chemist Justus von Liebig in the protein casein from cheese. It is called tyrosyl when referred to as a functional group or side chain.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The sugar present in DNA is :
questions.explanation: The deoxyribose is sugar found in DNA. It is a variant of five carbon sugar called ribose. The DNA is an informational molecule found mainly in the nucleus of the cell.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Who has proposed for the first time the double helix model of DNA ?
questions.explanation: James Dewey Watson (born April 6, 1928) was an American molecular biologist, geneticist and zoologist, best known as one of the co-discoverers of the structure (double helix model) of DNA in 1953 with Francis Crick. Watson, Crick, and Maurice Wilkins were awarded the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their discoveries concerning the "molecular structure of nucleic acids (DNA) and its significance for information transfer in living material". * James D. Watson and Francis Crick are associated with the discovery of [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2012] - Structure of DNA

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How many chromosomes are there in humans?
questions.explanation: In humans, each cell normally contains 23 pairs of chromosomes, a total of 46. Twenty-two of these pairs called autosomes which are the same in both males and females. The 23rd pair, the sex chromosomes differ between males and females. Females have two copies of the X chromosome (XX) while males have one X and one Y chromosome (XY).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following does not have sex-chromosome?
questions.explanation: Karyotypes of many species of the genus Sceloporus support the generalization that there are no morphologically recognizable sex chromosomes in lizards.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a source of bio-fertilizer?
questions.explanation: Azolla has the capability of nitrogen-fixing. That is why it is being widely used as a biofertilizer, especially in parts of Southeast Asia.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is/are used as biofertilizers? Select the correct answer from the codes 2given below: 1. Azolla 2. Blue-green algae 3. Alfalfa 4. Nitrolin Codes :
questions.explanation: Biofertilizers are defined as preparations containing living cells or latent cells of efficient strains of microorganisms that help crop plants uptake of nutrients, by their interactions in the rhizosphere when applied through seed or soil. They accelerate certain microbial processes in the soil which augment the extent of availability of nutrients in a form easily assimilated by plants. They can be grouped in different ways based on their nature and function. Nitrogen-fixing Biofertilizer : Azotobacter, Beijerinkia, Clostridium, Klebsiella, Anabaena, Nostoc, Rhizobium, Frankia, Anabaena azollae. Phosphorus-solubilizing/mobilizing Biofertilizers : Bacillus megatherium var. phosphaticum, Aspergillus, Pezizella ericae. Biofertilizers for micronutrients : Bacillus spp. Plant Growth Promoting Rhizobacteria : Pseudomonas fluorescence. Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) and Azolla are used as biofertilizers. However, Alfalfa is a perennial flowering plant of the pea family.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra UPPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which ofthe following is not a nitrogen-fixing organism?
questions.explanation: Nostoc, Anabaena and Azotobacter are nitrogen-fixing organisms while mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between a fungus and a plant.

questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria or blue-green algae is an example of biofertilizer, which helps in fixing atmospheric nitrogen. Blue-green algae are mainly used as biofertilizer in the crop paddy.

questions.explanation: Blue-green algae is also called Cyanobacteria. It is associated with biological nitrogen fixation.
